# Decisions D-0–D-249

Part of [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md), which lists every part. Entries keep their order; this part holds the numbers D-0–D-249.

<!-- entries -->
- **D-1 (U-15).** The name "AER" is kept and is always expanded as "AgentPROV Execution Record".
- **D-2 (U-07).** The large acquisitions are approved and done. They sit in the verified cache under
  `~/.agentprov/cache/` (see AGENTS.md §0). All 18,234 baseline legacy logs are byte-identical to
  `ethz-spylab/agentdojo@c274885`.
- **D-3 (U-02).** w3id registration is carried out:
  - the public target repo `nickjones39/agentprov-ns` (GitHub Pages) serves `https://nickjones39.github.io/agentprov-ns/`,
    with `ns/apv.ttl` as a *draft* namespace declaration, `0.1.0-draft`;
  - PR `perma-id/w3id.org#6836` adds `ids/agentprov/.htaccess`: `/ns` uses 303 content negotiation;
    `/exec/` returns 302 to an explanation page; everything else returns 302 with the path preserved;
  - the versioned `/ns/<x.y.z>` rules were added to PR #6836 itself on 2026-10-08, when phase 5 published apv 0.1.0
    to `agentprov-ns` (the PR was still unmerged, so a second PR depending on it was not opened).

  Corpora carrying `https://w3id.org/agentprov/` IRIs MUST NOT be deposited before that PR is merged and
  resolves.
- **D-4 (U-01).** AgentDojo-PROV v2.3 is **not** deposited now. The existing AgentDojo-PROV Zenodo concept
  (`10.5281/zenodo.20692312`, latest v2.2) is left untouched. AgentPROV cites the baseline by framework
  commit `579a908`.
  *Superseded in fact by D-900 (2026-10-28): the user deposited v2.3 under that concept on 2026-10-10.*
- **D-5 (Zenodo for AgentPROV).** AgentPROV corpora get a **brand-new Zenodo record and concept DOI**.
  They are never a new version of the AgentDojo-PROV concept. The release builder (`release/`) MUST
  provide an upload script that:
  - reads the user's own `ZENODO_TOKEN` from the environment (the token is never handled, logged or
    stored by AgentPROV tooling or by coding agents);
  - creates a **new deposition** as an **unpublished draft** with deterministic archives, checksums and
    metadata;
  - leaves publication to the user, who presses Publish in the Zenodo web UI after review.
- **D-6 (2026-10-08, uv upgraded).** The user upgraded uv to 0.12.23, and CPython 3.14.8 is installed. As
  G.7.1(1) and MN M.2 foresaw, the committed floor is raised to `required-version = ">=0.12.22"`. This
  supersedes C-1's `>=0.12.18`, and the backend projects of phase 2 use the same floor. The core
  development environment runs on 3.14.8, and `prov` 3.2.2, `rdflib` 7.6.0 and `pyshacl` 0.40.1 import
  there. AD-16 (c) is otherwise unchanged: `requires-python = ">=3.14"`, and the `envinfo.py` release-mode
  guard below 3.14.8 still protects installs on older 3.14 patches. The spec's observations of uv 0.12.18
  (obs-M1, obs-G14) remain correct as historical records.
- **D-7 (2026-10-08, platform agnosticism; user requirement, architect ruling).** AgentPROV MUST run on Linux,
  macOS and Windows, on x86_64 and arm64. Platform handling is **capability-based**:
  - `agentprov.host` (L0) probes the host once per process. `detect_host() -> HostProfile` holds the facts (OS
    family, release, normalised arch, CPU count, physical memory, page size) and the **probed** capabilities
    (rlimits present and *enforced*, RSS sampler `procfs | libproc | psapi | none`, process-tree kill `killpg | job
    object`, hard memory cap `RLIMIT_AS | job object`). Each capability records how it was decided. Code tests
    capabilities, never OS names, and no platform constant (page size, flags) is hard-coded.
  - `constants_for(profile, calibration) -> HostConstants` is a **pure** function that sets the watchdog interval,
    the RSS trigger margin and the default worker count. Without a hard memory cap, a short, bounded
    memory-bandwidth calibration in a T1 worker sizes the margin. Nothing is cached on disk.
  - **Isolation grade** `enforced | watchdog | degraded`. Release mode requires at least `watchdog`; below it,
    exit 3 (`worker.isolation.insufficient`). Dev mode warns and records the grade. This mirrors AD-16.
  - The profile, capabilities, constants, calibration and grade are recorded in the `corpus.json` producer block.
    They never enter AER, SEM or PROV bytes, which MUST be byte-identical on every platform (binary I/O, `\n` line
    ends, no locale encodings).
  - The CI `core` job runs on `ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `macos-latest` and `windows-latest`.
  - **Added 2026-10-08 (first CI run):** three more probed capabilities, each with its "how decided": `nofollow`
    (`native | verify_identity | none`, selected once in `ingest.paths._probe`, G.3.10(13)), `posix_permissions` (chmod
    bits read back; G.4.12(7)) and `startup_vm_bytes` (the floor under `RLIMIT_AS`; G.4.12(8)). Tests skip on
    capabilities, and no source file other than `ingest/paths.py` names `O_NOFOLLOW`.
  - **Scope:** the live backends' T2 OS sandbox (G.4.10) stays per-platform and is decided at phase 8.
  - **Rejected:** `sys.platform` branches with per-OS constants. They are brittle on new hardware and cannot tell
    "accepts setrlimit" from "enforces it", which is exactly macOS's `RLIMIT_AS` behaviour. A `psutil` dependency was
    also rejected: it is a compiled third-party package in the tier-1 safety path, and it is not needed.
- **D-8 (2026-10-08, live feedback; user requirement, architect ruling).** Long-running commands, live trace runs
  above all, give levelled live feedback on stderr: `--progress off|summary|status|steps|trace`, formats
  `tty|plain|jsonl` and an optional `--progress-file`, specified in MN N.1.14. Feedback is metadata only by default;
  `--show-content` adds escaped excerpts. It is a separate channel from logging. The binding guarantees:
  - feedback never changes evidence bytes (F1);
  - the capture never waits on the display: bounded, droppable queues, a dedicated pipe reader and a throttled
    renderer (F2);
  - overhead is measured and reported (F3);
  - no decision reads the level (F4).

  **Rejected:**
  - routing progress through `logging`: handler I/O runs synchronously in the emitting thread, which would let a
    slow terminal back-pressure the capture;
  - a third-party progress library such as `rich` or `tqdm`: a new core dependency, and terminal-escape handling
    over untrusted strings.
- **D-9 (2026-10-08, trace concurrency; user requirement, architect ruling).** `agentprov run --jobs N` sets the
  number of concurrent traces (backend workers). The baseline hard-coded 18. The rules (MN N.1.10(1)):
  - the default is 1, and N ≥ 1;
  - N above the host maximum (D-7 memory budget) is refused with that maximum named; it is never clamped silently;
  - `--start-stagger SECONDS` is a deterministic start spread that replaces the baseline's random sleep;
  - both values are recorded with the run.

  **Rejected:** a fixed default above 1 (paid endpoints), and an env-var default (hidden configuration of paid,
  recorded runs).
- **D-10 (2026-10-08, local models and the `m5ultra` preset; user requirement, architect ruling).** Local
  OpenAI-compatible servers are first-class live endpoints: `ollama` is kept, and `omlx` (oMLX on Apple Silicon,
  `127.0.0.1:8000/v1`) is added. `--preset m5ultra` (shorthand `--m5ultra`) targets the user's Mac Studio M5 Ultra
  (80-core GPU, 256 GB). Unless `--jobs` is given, its concurrency is **computed from the model**:
  `min(J_compute(active params), J_memory(weights, KV per trace), J_server)` (MN N.2.1a). The table values are
  provisional, from published oMLX and SiliconBench data. They are calibrated on the machine with `--tune-jobs` in
  phase 8.

  **Rejected:**
  - a fixed number such as 4 or 18: concurrency depends on the model's size and context;
  - a hard-coded per-OS preset logic: presets are package data, consistent with D-7.
- **D-11 (2026-10-08, artefact controls for live capture; user requirement, architect ruling).** The 13 artefact
  classes of the AgentDojo-PROV generated corpus are addressed in D.10.9.
  - **Principle:** never alter an execution to hide an artefact. Harness causes are removed by construction.
    Known-bad configurations are refused by **preflight probes** (parameter transmission, structured tool calls,
    accepted roles, server reachability). A **canary** of 10 cells, on by default, stops a misconfigured campaign
    early. What still occurs is flagged with evidence-class-I notes and seal issues, live and in a capture-quality
    report.
  - **New choices:** `--temperature-policy as-benchmark|inject` is required when a configured parameter would not be
    transmitted. `--allow-text-tool-calls` is required to run an endpoint that returns text-encoded tool calls.
  - **Kept deferred:** the replay-based cell probes for benchmark-validity defects (A13; AD-10 as ruled), pending the
    user's decision.
  - **Rejected:**
    - silent fixes, such as re-sending temperature or resampling text tool calls: they are observer effects of
      exactly the kind the baseline's `_CompatLLM` introduced;
    - discarding artefact traces: that is the selection artefact A11.
- **D-12 (2026-10-08, artefact catalogues for every source; user requirement, architect ruling).** Every source that
  becomes an AgentPROV PROV corpus gets a versioned artefact catalogue (`adapters/<family>/artefacts.toml`). The
  sources include the AgentDojo legacy runs (the converted corpus), the AgentDojo-PROV trees, ROPE and AutoDojo, the
  NIST mirror, AgentDyn, Mandate, DRIFT, the survey sources, CIAware-Bench, STAC and live capture.
  - **Mechanism:** the handling is **per source and bespoke**. Each adapter owns its catalogue and handles every
    edge case at conversion time, through its own mapper, profile and SEM rules; the pattern repeats in every
    input source. A thin shared layer, `agentprov.artefacts` (L3; it changes no protected package), holds only the
    catalogue schema, a source-neutral safety net over AER and the reports. Hits that no catalogue entry claims are recorded as `artefact.unclassified.*`, never
    dropped. Inspection is proactive (`import --dry-run --artefacts`) and reporting is per-source (`stats
    --artefacts`, numbers-only reports feeding the manuscript).
  - **Cleaning** is limited to five declared classes (D.15.1): correct representation, derived reconstruction by a
    declared rule, recomputed judgements beside the recorded ones (SEM and the assessment bundle), flag only, and
    not recoverable. Raw bytes, AER source values and the compat oracle are never changed.
  - **Converted AgentDojo runs:** their handling is recorded entry by entry in D.15.5.
  - **Rejected:**
    - "cleaning" by rewriting values or dropping traces: it destroys evidence and creates selection artefacts;
    - per-adapter ad-hoc flags with no shared catalogue schema: the counts would not be comparable across sources,
      nor citable in the paper;
    - one central artefact engine holding source knowledge: it would break invariants 1 and 9.
- **D-13 (2026-10-08, the engine agent is version-free; user delegated the choice, implementation ruling).** PROV
  documents name the AgentPROV engine `sw:agentprov`, with `apv:softwareName` but no version. The software version
  and code digest of each run are recorded once per corpus in `derivation.json` (H.8.2: `engine`,
  `engine_code_sha256`). Adapters keep `sw:<adapter-id>.<version>`, because the adapter version is in the AER header
  and therefore an input of `derive`.
  - **Why:** E.3.4 item 3 and E.9 require byte-identical PROV-JSON for fixed AER, spec, catalogue and options. A
    version in the document would change every digest at every release, even one that changes no semantics, so
    `recompute --check` could never pass across releases.
  - **Rejected:**
    - keeping `sw:agentprov.<version>`: every patch release becomes a recompute failure;
    - putting the software version into `dk`: every release mints new bundle IRIs, contradicting E.3.4 item 3;
    - naming the engine by spec version (`sw:agentprov.agentprov-prov-0.1`): redundant with the derive activity's plan
      `rules:agentprov-prov.0.1`.
- **D-14 (2026-10-08, the phase-6 freeze of `aer/0.1` and `capture/0.1`; AD-06 executed).** Three importers were built
  against the formats before they froze: the Inspect `.eval` importer (D.9; 6 survey AgentHarm logs, 1,056 samples),
  the AgentDojo TraceLogger `v0.k11` importer (D.6; all 18,241 pinned logs at `c274885`, full gate R passing) and the
  FooBench future-framework adapter (D.12). None needed a new record kind, field or enum value. Two core changes were
  made before the freeze, both corrections recorded in C.20: cached agent calls answer the agent in
  `aer.acc.agent_calls_vs_assistant@1`, and adapter families are discovered by convention instead of from core name
  tables. `capture/0.1` gained its published schema (C.13.9). From this date the published schemas, the 13 record
  kinds and the closed enums are pinned by `tests/unit/test_format_freeze.py` (`versions.FROZEN`).
  - **Rule:** any change to a frozen format is a new version (`aer/0.2`, `capture/0.2`) with its own schema file,
    reader support for both, a DECISIONS entry and an AGENTS.md record (D.12.4); a pin is never updated in place.
    Seal issue codes (`CORE_ISSUE_CODES`) stay validator vocabulary and are not pinned.
  - **Rejected:** freezing before the three importers landed (the FooBench test found two core name tables that would
    have forced a core edit per framework, and the Inspect fixtures found the cached-call accounting gap); and freezing
    the validator's issue vocabulary with the record grammar (it would turn every new diagnostic into a format bump).
- **D-15 (2026-10-08, unpinned `--input` is refused in v0.1; user delegated the choice, implementation ruling).**
  `agentprov import --input` requires `--verify-against-pin` (or the pin is read with `--fetch`); otherwise exit 4,
  `raw.origin.local`. MN N.2.2 is amended: its "local origin with a notice" path is withdrawn for v0.1.
  - **Why:** every corpus claim rests on re-verifiable origins (git blob id or listing digest against a pin); a `local`
    origin names only "a file on this machine", and release mode already refuses a corpus carrying one (HL origin
    table), so an unpinned working corpus could never be sealed: refusing at the door is the honest behaviour. Every
    registered source has a pin, so a pinned path always exists. Supporting `local` would need a mode-dependent AER
    writer, new core behaviour straight after the freeze, for no v0.1 use case.
  - **Where unpinned data goes instead:** a new source gets a profile with pins (an adapter's job); AgentPROV's own runs
    are live capture (phase 8), whose `capture` origin is self-recording.
  - **Rejected:** a mode-dependent writer accepting `local` in dev mode (unsealable corpora, core change);
    accepting unpinned files silently (unverifiable evidence). Revisitable as an explicit, documented
    `--allow-unpinned` dev flag if a real need appears.

- **D-16 (2026-10-08, a request-less tool execution gets no exposure assessment; spec conflict, implementation ruling).**
  D.12.2 and K.6.4 list "exposure assessment with subject `x:te5`" for FooBench's text-parsed action (phase 7), but EF
  E.7.3, which owns the assessment mapping, says a `tool_execution` without a request part has no generating invocation
  and therefore no context premise in `aer/0.1`: no exposure is emitted and the count is reported. EF governs. `te5`
  gets no `apv:ExposedTo` (nor taint); the derivation report counts it, and K.6.4 asserts the absence as a named gap.
  - **Why:** exposure is a claim about the context of the invocation that generated the request. `te5` records only
    `requested_by: "agent"`; nothing links it to the assistant message it was parsed from, so any context would be
    guessed, which invariant 2 forbids. The role and integrity labels of `te5` are still emitted.
  - **Rejected:** taking the context of the nearest earlier invocation of the requesting actor (an order-based guess);
    adding a `parsed_from` link (an `aer/0.1` change after the freeze, D-14). Revisitable in `aer/0.2` with an explicit
    source link for text-parsed actions.
- **D-17 (2026-10-08, the published apv 0.1.0 gains no term in phase 7; implementation ruling).** The assessment rule
  `aprov.a_payload@1` needs an `apv:assumption` on an `ambiguous` injection-marker claim (EF E.7.3). It takes it from
  the SEM profile's catalogue: the marker rule or normaliser the annotation cites must declare one (for
  `agentdojo.suites@1`: `agentdojo:NormaliserRejectionIsContainment`, on `agentdojo.injection_marker_ambiguous@1`), and
  an ambiguous marker whose rules declare none is refused (`prov.sem_invalid`). The phase-7 engine's first cut added a
  core individual `apv:UndecodedMarkerMatch`; it was reverted.
  - **Why:** apv 0.1.0 is published (`nickjones39/agentprov-ns`, w3id PR #6836), and E.4.6 allows term additions only
    in a minor version. A 0.2.0 would change `apv:vocabularyVersion` in every document (every PROV digest) and needs a
    republish with the user's consent, for a term whose meaning is profile-specific anyway (which normaliser rejected
    what). Adapter-declared assumptions are already strings in PROV (EF E.10 item 11).
  - **Rejected:** editing 0.1.0 in place (E.4.6 forbids it; published IRIs would change meaning); bumping to 0.2.0
    now (every digest changes for one term); emitting the ambiguous claim without an assumption (E.7.3 requires one).
- **D-18 (2026-10-08, the v2.3 scoring rule set and gate C3 stay out of phase 7; implementation ruling).**
  `agentdojo.scoring@1/@2` (the v2.3 `score_trace` rules as SEM annotations) and gate C3 are not built in phase 7; the
  names `agentdojo.scoring`, `account_confound`, `text_tool_call` and `unwinnable_cell` stay `reserved` in the
  `agentdojo` catalogue.
  - **Why:** the PQ phase-7 DoD does not include them. `score_trace` reads `outcome_replay.json` rows (replay evidence),
    and outcome replay is deferred (AD-10 row 2); C3 belongs to K's `old-vs-new` job, which does not exist yet (C2 and
    C5 are not built either), and gate C is a port-fidelity diagnostic, not a release gate (AD-07).
  - **Where it goes:** with the `old-vs-new` job (C2, C3, C5, C6), when the baseline environment probe is wired into
    CI or a local gate command. Until then the paper states no port-fidelity fact about scoring (J.3.4).
  - **Addendum (2026-10-12, regeneration-batch item 19; user-approved; the gate-C3 split agreed with the deferrals
    session).** `agentdojo.scoring@1` (`score_trace` at `579a908`, verbatim) and `@2` (`@1` plus F-60: `unwinnable` and
    `rerun_not_reproduced` for targeted injections only) are built as a **library** rule set,
    `adapters/agentdojo/semantics/scoring.py` `score(rec, row, *, run_error, rule_set) -> Verdict`, which gate C3's
    comparer (the deferrals session's, in `migration/`) calls; `derive` does not, so no AER, SEM or PROV record carries a
    verdict. `scoring` (both versions), `account_confound` and `unwinnable_cell` become `active`, the last two as the
    rules a verdict's `unscored_reason` (`account`, `unwinnable`) cites; `text_tool_call` stays `reserved` (`score_trace`
    never reads it). Only the `agentdojo` catalogue digest moves. **Rejected:** SEM emission of the D.15.5 annotations
    now (C3 does not need them; it would change SEM where they fire and needs its own prediction); a `rec` builder in
    the adapter (the comparer builds `rec` from AER and SEM beside the gate code it belongs to).
  - **Also recorded:** `inspect.agentharm@1` labels every AgentHarm tool `unknown` (fail-closed): the tool list is not
    available offline, so the profile states outcomes (judge scores and scales) and no taint policy.
- **D-19 (2026-10-08, live facts outside the closed `capture/0.1` payloads go into `note` events; implementation
  ruling, phase 8).** The harness records, as namespaced `note` events, the facts that the frozen event payloads cannot
  hold: `instrumentation_observed` (resample and retry counts, which exist only after the passes, while
  `instrumentation` must be the second event), `identity_digests` (RECORD, guarded-source and lock digests; the
  `identity` payload is closed), `cell`, `pipeline`, `wire_headers` (the redacted header names and allowlisted values)
  and `native_log_stock_path`. The capture mapper maps `instrumentation_observed` into the item's `params.observed`
  (D.10.7) and keeps the others in raw only (D.10.4a). Reasoning and refusal text, which stock AgentDojo keeps out of
  its message list, are mapped from the kept response blob as `O:provider` parts (D.10.4a items 28–33).
  - **Why:** `capture/0.1` froze in phase 6 (D-14), and C.13.3 reserves `note` for adapter facts.
  - **Rejected:** widening `identity` or `instrumentation` in place (a format change after the freeze); a
    `capture/0.2` for facts that `note` already carries; writing the observed counts into a later second
    `instrumentation` event (C.13.3 fixes its position).
- **D-20 (2026-10-08, a worker-reported digest that does not verify is a register row; implementation ruling, phase
  8).** D.11.3 rule 2 asks for the AER seal issue `capture_error` when an artefact hash in `cell_done` does not verify.
  T0 instead stores the files under their actual digests and writes register row `map.capture_error` naming the label.
  The mapper still raises `capture_unsealed` and `capture_error` for what it can check in the evidence itself: the
  chain, a native log missing from the session (blobs and the native log are looked up by the digest the log
  records), and an unreadable pass dump. A referenced request or response blob missing from the session is not yet
  a seal issue: the call keeps its blob reference and loses only the checks that read it (sent transforms, alignment
  without `input_at`). This is an open item (AGENTS.md §0).
  - **Why:** the mismatch is a fact about the worker's report on the protocol channel, which never enters raw
    evidence, so the mapper cannot observe it. The register is where T0's ingestion facts live (HL H.6).
  - **Rejected:** passing T0's verdict into the mapper as an extra input (mapping would then depend on something
    outside the raw evidence, against invariant 6); a new catalogue rule for an issue the AER cannot justify.
- **D-21 (2026-10-08, gate C6 compares against stock-by-default behaviour; implementation ruling, phase 8).** C6 passes
  14/14 scenarios with six registered differences: the four B.9/D.7.3 deviations J.3.4 names (F-02, F-05, F-13, D.7.3),
  plus `XD-C6-D105-benign-security` (the stock benign-task function sets `security: true` by `harness_default`, where
  the old generator wrote `null`) and `XD-C6-C153-generator-meta` (the old generator's `meta.model`/`meta.model_config`
  bookkeeping has no observed counterpart in a live AER). The wire requests of `gateway_compat` equal the old
  generator's in every scenario. The stock 0.1.35 rendering of the system message as `developer` is not a sent
  transform; only the `gateway_compat` rewrite back to `system` is (`role_rewrite`).
  - **Why:** D5 makes stock behaviour the reference, and gate C measures port fidelity, not correctness (AD-07). A view
    rule that rebuilt the old `meta` members would fabricate values that were never observed (invariant 2).
  - **Rejected:** calling the old generator's benign path from the backend to reproduce `null` (a non-stock harness);
    a live render rule for `meta.model_config` (the element's default temperature and the `provider_default` label are
    not recorded).
- **D-22 (2026-10-11, no scheduled CI; network-rebuilding jobs by manual dispatch at release, deposit and submission
  points; user decision).** AgentPROV has no scheduled or nightly CI of any kind. The feature is removed from the
  architecture, not deferred. Push and pull-request CI is unchanged. The jobs that rebuild pinned environments from the
  network, or run the slow gates (`backend-autodojo`, `old-vs-new`, `network` and `thorough`; the latter two are built
  when their gates have tests), run by `workflow_dispatch` only. K.19.1 defines the points at which they are
  dispatched: before tagging a software release; before building or depositing a corpus release (depositing also needs
  the user's explicit instruction, D-5); before submitting a thesis chapter or paper that reports live-backend or
  migration results; and after changing what they exercise (`backends/**`, `capture/**`, a backend `uv.lock`, the
  baseline lock in `migration/`, the gate-C6 register, the `agentdojo` capture mapping). The supply-chain workflow runs
  on changes to any `uv.lock` and by manual dispatch. The Hypothesis `nightly` profile (K.3.4) is renamed `thorough`:
  an on-demand profile run locally or by dispatch, with no code yet.
  - **Why:** this is a single-researcher project and external pins rarely change. What matters is that the pinned
    environments rebuild at the points where the work claims they can, and a failure there (fork rewritten, wheel
    yanked, file moved) is then reported as a finding, not re-pinned silently.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a nightly schedule: it re-ran the full four-OS matrix every night and duplicated push CI, at the cost of GitHub
      Actions minutes on a private repository;
    - a weekly schedule: the same duplication at a lower rate.
  - **Supersedes:** the schedule trigger, the "nightly" columns and profile, and the "weekly" supply-chain run of K.3.4,
    K.3.5, K.18.1 and K.19; K.20 item 1; MN M.7 and N.2.14; G.7.2 and G.10 (SEC-23); and the "optional nightly" gate C1
    of J.2.6, J.3.4 and J.8 (RM-22).
- **D-23 (2026-10-11, lone surrogates in source text are handled in the adapter layer, never by a format change; user
  decision, implemented with the regeneration batch).** A lone UTF-16 surrogate in source text (escaped `\ud83d` from a
  truncated emoji, or in an object key) currently makes the whole execution a degenerate `adapter_defect` AER, because
  `aer.canon.encode_value` emits `$utf16` and the typed `text` field rejects it (escaping audit F-01,
  `docs/reports/analysis/research/A4-escaping.md`). No record of the current corpora is affected (0 degenerate units).
  The fix keeps `aer/0.1` frozen: no `$utf16` in typed text fields, no `aer/0.2`. The implementer chooses the best
  approach within these constraints when the batch is built; the preferred design is a shared adapter-layer helper
  that replaces each lone surrogate in text and keys by U+FFFD and discloses it (a D-class rule, e.g.
  `ingest.lone_surrogate_replaced@1`, with the JSON pointer and a reference to the unchanged raw bytes), so nothing is
  lost (the raw store keeps the original) and the execution is mapped instead of degenerate. It is implemented in the
  regeneration batch (`docs/reports/analysis/regen-batch.md`) because the new rule changes a rule catalogue, whose
  digest every PROV document carries.
  - **Why:** a single malformed character should not discard an otherwise observable execution, and a replacement is
    defensible only when it is disclosed and the original stays recoverable.
  - **Rejected:** `aer/0.2` with `$utf16` allowed in text (every AER digest of every corpus changes for a case absent
    from the data); silently dropping or replacing the character (undisclosed loss, invariant 2); a separate catalogue
    cited only when the rule fires (avoids one regeneration but adds machinery for an edge case; reconsider only if the
    batch is otherwise empty).
- **D-24 (2026-10-11, a D-class rule is cited only for code its verification lists; unverified harnesses get class-I
  twins; user decision C6, implemented with the regeneration batch).** D.5.4's citation rule applies to every D-class
  rule, not only the structural ones: a profile whose harness code is not verified (`code_identity` `unpinned` or
  `range`, e.g. ROPE, AgentDyn, and head `v1.k14` / Mandate where the cited code is only at `c274885`) cites the rule's
  `_unverified` twin at class I, which moves the statement into the inference bundle. The most consequential case is
  the retry inference (analysis B6: ROPE 322, AgentDyn 826 executions become `unverifiable` instead of
  `known_incomplete`). D.5.4 is clarified accordingly when the batch is built.
  - **Why:** a derived statement must rest on verified code; for unverified harnesses the same logic is an inference.
  - **Rejected:** limiting the rule to the structural rules (keeps D-class claims that the evidence does not support).
- **D-25 (2026-10-11, licence exclusion criteria for the systematic source search; user decision).** A source is
  converted only if its data is under a licence that permits redistributing derived data. Records with **no licence**
  (EX-LIC-1) and records whose licence **forbids redistribution**, including evaluation-only licences (EX-LIC-2), are
  excluded, however well their format fits. A repository-level licence that covers the data counts as a licence (MIT by
  repository for AgentDojo upstream, ROPE and AgentDyn). A use clause that still permits redistribution (AgentHarm) is
  included with the clause recorded (U-05). Copyleft and non-commercial licences permit redistribution and are
  included (user decision, same day): GPL-3.0 and AGPL-3.0 sources each become their own corpus under that licence,
  and CC-BY-NC sources go into a separate `-nc` corpus under the existing `nc_partition` policy. Every screened record, included or excluded, appears in the manuscript's
  included/excluded table with its licence and exclusion code. The full criteria are in
  `docs/reports/systematic-search/eligibility-criteria.md`. In the registry, an excluded record keeps the existing
  vocabulary (`reference`/`forbidden`, role `mirror`/`not_executions`); "excluded" is not a registry status (§I.0.2).
  - **Why:** a corpus built from data with no licence, or a non-redistributable licence, cannot be published or
    deposited, and a complete table makes the source selection defensible.
  - **Rejected:** converting unlicensed data for local analysis only (the results could not be reproduced from a
    published corpus); treating a missing platform licence tag as "no licence" without reading the LICENSE file or
    README (would wrongly exclude sources licensed at repository level).
- **D-26 (2026-10-11, phase 10b: DTap-Bench is added as a new adapter family before phase 11; user decision).** The
  systematic search found DTap-Bench (`AI-Secure/DTap-Bench-Agent-Trajectories` @ `836caf2f…`, Apache-2.0): 67,808
  trajectory files, 65,902 judge results and 6,682 task configurations over 10 agent-framework/model pairs, covering
  four agent frameworks (OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Google ADK, OpenClaw), 14 domains, and direct and
  indirect injection. (Full census of 2026-10-11, `dtap-bench.md` §6; the first listing counted only the 64,110
  timestamp-named trajectory files.) It is the only large, licensed, non-AgentDojo agent-security source found.
  Phase 10b adds a `dtap` adapter family in four steps: verification and source card; spec (new D section, I_matrix
  card); implementation; then the full import and its reports. Task configurations come from
  `AI-Secure/DecodingTrust-Agent-Platform` @ `a3edc9b7…` (Apache-2.0) and are joined per run. The join is verified by
  task id, instruction and malicious goal, and a mismatch is disclosed.
  - **Limitation (manuscript):** tool-description (and skill or prompt) injections are often not observable in DTap's
    run logs, which record tool descriptions and system prompts only for some harnesses (OpenClaw tool lists, debug
    logs). For 3,533 of 6,162 successful indirect attacks (57.3%) the payload appears neither in a tool output nor in
    a logged tool description. Payloads are recovered from the pinned task configuration, and exposure to them is
    recorded as a class-I inference, never as an observation (`docs/reports/systematic-search/candidates/dtap-bench.md`
    §6, which corrects §4's two-run sample).
  - **Why before phase 11:** phases 11–15 add no sources. The new family's catalogue is embedded only in the PROV of
    executions that declare it (`prov/rules/top.py:129-137`), so no existing corpus digest changes and the
    regeneration batch is unaffected. Phases 11–13 (datasheet, licence-class packaging, fuzzing, full regression) and
    the manuscript then cover it.
  - **Rejected:** deferring to after v0.1.0 (it would miss phase 11–13 coverage and the manuscript numbers); reading
    only the environment-injection runs (that hides the limitation instead of measuring it).
- **D-27 (2026-10-11, examination-2 rulings c1–c6; user decision on the recommendations).**
  - (c1) The AgentDyn datasheet flags the gemini-2.5-flash undefended baseline (separate generation window).
  - (c2) Execution ids stay content-addressed: the same run in two corpora has the same id, and pooled analyses
    deduplicate by id. `x:` IRIs are not scoped by corpus.
  - (c3) The Inspect run/step activities and the harness agent are connected by a D rule where the inspect_ai code
    supports it; otherwise the isolation is documented.
  - (c4) A D rule attributes each AgentHarm sample's input messages to the benchmark, citing the task definition.
  - (c5) The datasheet states that delegation associations and attribution generators are implied by PROV inferences,
    not asserted.
  - (c6) Documentary evidence alone is not enough for class D: the nine document-only D rules get `_unverified`
    class-I twins under D-24.
  - c3, c4 and c6 change corpus content and are items of the regeneration batch (`docs/reports/analysis/regen-batch.md`);
    c1, c2 and c5 are datasheet statements (`docs/reports/analysis/datasheet-items.md`, applied by phase 11).
  - **Why:** c2 keeps identity tied to content, which is what makes deduplication possible; c6 keeps class D to
    verified code, as D-24 requires; c3/c4 connect statements only where code evidence exists.
  - **Rejected:** corpus-scoped execution ids (two ids for identical bytes); keeping document-only rules at class D.
- **D-28 (2026-10-11, the `dtap` adapter family: design rulings for DTap-Bench; phase 10b step 2, spec §D.16).**
  Recorded so that implementation (step 3) and review can check the design against its reasons.
  - (a) **Own family.** DTap gets a new family (`dtap.trajectory` reader and mapper, profile `dtap-bench`, catalogue
    `dtap` v1, semantics `dtap.tools@1`) rather than a profile of `agentdojo` or `inspect`. Its step log has no message
    list, no model-call boundary and no call ids, and its payloads live in a second dataset.
  - (b) **Identity.** The execution id is content-addressed (AD-04, D-27 c2). The logical identity is the path plus
    file stem; `task_info.task_id` and `trace_id` are never identity (both are non-unique), and the model and harness
    come from the path only.
  - (c) **Pairing is class I for all four harnesses, strict alternation included (D-24).** The logs carry no call id,
    so every pairing rule rests on how an unverified harness writes its log. The name check corroborates and never
    raises the class. Multi-call batches (8.6 % of results) are disclosed per batch.
  - (d) **Inferred model calls.** One `model_call` per maximal segment of agent steps (I), whose `input` is the logged
    prefix (I). The unlogged system prompt and tool descriptions are never input members; a logged tool list is a
    fixture referenced by `tools` (I).
  - (e) **Role `agent` is kept verbatim**, so the role-`assistant` accounting and typing do not apply.
  - (f) **Time.** `traj_info.timestamp` is the run end at class I (a statistical fit). The naive googleadk times are
    `end_naive` with `ambiguous`. Durations without a clock go to `ext` with `/t/dur_s` `ambiguous`. No start and no
    per-step time is computed.
  - (g) **Configuration join.** A deterministic path join and a deterministic tier (A, B, C). Configuration content
    describes a run only in tier A, and always at class I (never O). Id normalisations are applied only where
    evidenced, and only to the recorded `task_id` check.
  - (h) **Injection exposure.** A payload is *observed in the run* when a deterministic matcher (D) finds it in a field
    the run logs (tool output, logged tool-description list, logged user step); otherwise it is *configured only*, and
    every statement about it is class I. The configured payload entity, its attribution and its run membership are
    inference-bundle statements. The exposure claim (`dtap.exposure`, eight classes) is an assessment, as every
    exposure claim is (E.7.2), at class I for `configured_only`.
  - (i) **Judge evidence.** Recorded judge values are O; their `checker` origin is I (the judge code is not verified
    for the runs). `direct_prompt` `task_success` and benign null `attack_success` are `harness_default`.
  - (j) **Fixtures.** Configurations with `env_vars` are committed as derived fixtures, with their transformation and
    the original digest recorded. They are test inputs, never corpus raw.
  - **Why:** each choice states only what the files and the census support. Where the only premise is the behaviour
    of a harness whose code is unavailable, D-24 makes the statement an inference, and the observed/inferred line on
    exposure is exactly the line between text the run log holds and text only the configuration holds.
  - **Rejected:**
    - (a) a profile of the AgentDojo family: its reader, quirks and model-call rules assume message lists and ids.
    - (c) D for strict alternation: it would rest on unverified logging semantics. Name matching for claudesdk: its
      result names are unreliable. No pairing at all: that would discard 91.4 % of unambiguous links.
    - (d) one `model_call` per agent step: it asserts a turn boundary the log does not show. No `model_call` at all:
      it hides the agent's activity and removes the context premise of every engine exposure claim. Rebuilding the
      context with the configuration's system prompt: that is an unrecorded input.
    - (e) relabelling `agent` to `assistant`: D.15.1 forbids relabelling source fields.
    - (f) converting the naive times to UTC from the file-name stamp pattern: an inference presented as a time.
      `end − duration` as a start: a derived time over an unknown clock.
    - (g) a commit-date choice of configuration revision: no revision existed during any run. D for tier A: the
      revision in force is unverifiable.
    - (h) treating configured tool-description payloads as observed fixtures: that would hide the limitation D-26
      requires to be measured. Dropping them: that would hide it too.
    - (j) committing configurations with `env_vars` byte-identical: sandbox credential values would enter the
      repository. Omitting those configurations: it would lose the `direct_prompt`, control, multi-turn and
      medical-join fixtures.
  - **Addendum (2026-10-12, user delegated the decision): inferred times are never PROV times.** A time value whose
    reading is class I (e.g. DTap's `traj_info.timestamp` as the run end, D.16.18 item 1) stays in the AER verbatim
    (`t.raw`, with the I-class reading declared) and is available to `stats` and analysis, but `agentprov-prov/0.1`
    emits `prov:startTime`/`prov:endTime` only from O- or D-class times. The engine currently turns an I-class activity
    time into an inference-bundle entity carrying `prov:endTime`, which tier 4 rightly refuses (`PV-NE-6`). That path
    is a latent engine bug: no shipped corpus reaches it (every corpus passes tier 4). It is fixed by making the engine
    omit PROV time attributes for I-class times and raise a disclosed issue, with zero byte change to existing corpora
    (to be proven by the golden and compat gates); assigned to the regeneration-batch session as a small core fix,
    recorded here per invariant 5 (a correctness fix of the engine, not a change any adapter requires).
    - **Why:** invariant 2 forbids filling gaps, and a time whose meaning is only inferred is not evidence for a PROV
      timestamp; examination 2 (N7) already shows PROV activity times exist only where the source records them.
    - **Rejected:** letting the validator accept time attributes on inference-bundle entities (puts an unverified
      reading into PROV's temporal semantics and weakens PV-NE-6); typing the DTap time as D (D-24: the harness code
      that writes it is not verified).
    - **Implemented (2026-10-12, regeneration-batch session; invariant 5 record).**
      - **Change:** `prov/rules/nodes.py` `times()` skips a present `/t/start` or `/t/end` whose class is I. It writes
        no `prov:*Time` and no `apv:*TimeLexical`, and adds the disclosure `inferred_time_omitted` (`<rid>/t/<end>`) to
        the derivation report, never to the PROV bytes. E.5.3 item 7 says so.
      - **Zero byte change:**
        - No stored AER has an I-class time: 0 of the 218,412 present times of the phase-10 corpora (adprov-v1 164,888,
          AgentHarm 53,524; the other corpora carry none), and 0 in the earlier stored copies of both.
        - Nor do current mappings: 300 adprov-v1 executions re-mapped from raw with the current mappers give 0 of
          2,782. AgentHarm's mapping is byte-identical to the stored one (item 3).
        - The golden PROV/SEM pins and the frozen compat oracle are unchanged.
      - **Tests:** `tests/unit/prov/test_engine_tier4.py`: the `inferred_time` variant passes tier 4, and
        `test_an_inferred_time_is_never_a_prov_time` checks no end time in any bundle, the D start in the core
        bundle, the disclosure and tier 4. Both fail without the fix (PV-NE-6 / `pv.prov_structure`).
      - **Not done here:** DTap still writes its run end only as `t.raw.end` (D.16.18 item 1). Typing it as an
        I-class `t.end` is now safe, but it is an adapter change for the DTap session.
  - **Addendum 2 (2026-10-13, user-approved; regeneration-batch item 24; invariant 5 record): an inferred
    `unexecuted_tool_call` is pointed at.** When the seal issue `unexecuted_tool_call` cites a class-I rule
    (`dtap.call_without_result@1`; AgentOps' `agentops.fault_injection_unverified@1`, phase 10i README §9), the
    engine put `apv:dispatchStatus apv:NotDispatched` into an inference-bundle mention with no `apv:sourcePointer`.
    Tier 4 refuses that statement (`pv.linkage.pointer_missing`, `pv.linkage.basis_not_cited`), and it blocked
    555 in-scope AgentOps runs. The cause is an engine gap, not the mappings: the same issue under a D rule
    validates. The fix is a correctness fix of the engine and the linkage check, not a change an adapter requires.
    - **Change:** the issue is the attribute's premise. `prov/engine.py` gives it the field `seal/issues/<i>`, with
      the class and method of the issue's rule, and `validate/linkage.py` reads a pointed seal issue's `rule` as cited.
      Spec E.10 item 23 is amended.
    - **Rejected:** exempting the statement from the pointer check like `x:capture-profile` (it would still fail
      `basis_not_cited`, and the declaration is a single addressable premise); pointing at the request part (that
      record does not cite the rule); typing the adapters' rules D (the dispatch status is not recorded, so I is
      right).
    - **Zero byte change** to stored corpora and goldens: every stored `unexecuted_tool_call` cites a D rule, and a
      D attribute is a core statement without pointers. Proof: the golden, gate-D, C.16 and compat tests pass
      unchanged.

- **D-29 (2026-10-11, DTap quality problems: settled handling; user-approved, specified in §D.16).** These are the
  user's rulings, relayed by the phase-10b coordination on 2026-10-11. Only the secrets policy remains open
  (§D.16.13).
  1. **Synthetic trajectories (20, `synthetic: true`)** are never executions. The raw is stored, the file is registered
     `select.not_execution_artefact` (role `not_executions`), and it is counted in the disclosure. The judge of such a
     directory is registered the same way.
  2. **Harness failures (47 OpenClaw runs, judged anyway)** are imported as executions with run status `error`; the
     error is observed (class O). The recorded judgements are kept verbatim beside the seal issue
     `dtap.judgement_on_failed_run`. They are excluded from attack and utility rates by default and counted separately.
  3. **Empty trajectories (17)** are `outcome_only` executions (the ROPE precedent): no invented steps, seal issues
     `no_execution_observed` and `dtap.empty_trajectory`, recorded judgements kept.
  4. **LFS-pointer trajectories (2):** step 3 fetches the two LFS objects by their pinned oid, verifies the sha256
     against the pointer, and imports them normally (downloads approved for phase 10b). If an object is unavailable,
     the file is registered as unresolved and is not an execution.
  5. **Re-judged results (458 `audit_correction`):** both values are kept as recorded judgements (class O), each with
     its own date and source as recorded. The dataset's audit field marks the corrected one effective
     (`dtap.audit_correction_effective@1`, D, citing that field; `recomputed`, `revises` the original). Stats default
     to the corrected value and report both.
  6. **Re-runs (1,291 task directories, and the `_N` files) under one judge:** every attempt is its own execution. The
     judge is linked to an attempt only when its recorded snippets or metadata match exactly one attempt's logged
     content (`dtap.judge_attempt_by_content@1`, D, citing both files). Otherwise it attaches to the directory group,
     unresolved: those attempts have no per-run outcome, are excluded from per-run rates by default, and are
     disclosed.
  7. **`(1)` copies (8)** are byte-identical: one execution with two origins (SEC-19 precedent). Differing bytes
     would make a separate attempt under item 6.
  8. **The partial trajectory (1)** is imported with a truncation seal issue (`dtap.partial_trajectory`, plus
     `incomplete_run`), with no gap filling.
  9. **`direct_prompt` `task_success`** (a constant, not a result) is kept as recorded (`harness_default`), marked
     non-informative in SEM and the assessment, and excluded from utility rates.
  - **Spec-level additions** (consistent with the rulings; open question 2 in §D.16.17): a judge in a
    single-trajectory directory without a content match is linked at class I (`dtap.judge_dir_colocation@1`); a
    directory holding only a judge yields an `outcome_only` unit (D.2.8). The seal issues use the `dtap.` namespace
    (C.12.3 is closed), and the register codes reuse H.6.3's closed set, with `dtap.*` only in `detail`.
  - **Why:** nothing fabricated becomes an execution; every recorded value is kept, beside the issue that qualifies
    it; rates exclude what is not a run outcome without deleting it; and identity stays content-addressed.
  - **Rejected:** dropping harness failures or empty runs (selection bias, invariant 7); replacing the original
    judgement by the corrected one (destroys a recorded value); attaching one judge to every attempt (it asserts
    outcomes for attempts it may not have scored); importing synthetic trajectories with a flag (they are not
    executions of anything).
  - **10. Secrets (user decision, 2026-10-11): option A, include.** The user judges DTap's secret-like strings to be
    synthetic benchmark data; every execution is imported and deposited, nothing is withheld, and no per-execution
    flag is raised. Unchanged: raw bytes are never edited, `env_vars` never enter derived records (configuration field
    allowlist), values are never tested, and the datasheet carries one general statement that the corpus contains
    injection payloads and secret-like strings by design. The open questions of §D.16.17 (judge co-location class I,
    role `agent` verbatim, catalogue-declared `stats` exclusions, runner items R1–R3 with phase-12 consultation
    before `raw/`) are decided as recommended.
    - **Rejected:** B (withholding up to about 2,600 executions, skewing the deposit's CRM attack set); D (redaction
      in derived records would remove whole messages, since `aer/0.1` cannot express partial redaction).
  - **Addendum (2026-10-12, user decisions on the DTap sample-corpus check, questions c1-c4 of
    `docs/reports/analysis/dtap-sample-check.md` §9.2; the four fixes b1-b4 were approved the same day).**
    - **Q1. Shared `raw:` entities that two documents of one corpus describe differently: accepted and disclosed.** A
      content-addressed `raw:` entity carries attributes relative to the execution that cites it: `apv:originPath` (a
      judge file byte-identical across task directories) and `apv:artefactRole` (a re-run attempt that is one
      execution's `primary` and a sibling's `supporting` artefact). Merging the documents of a corpus gives
      multi-valued attributes. That is valid PROV, as for the cross-corpus `apv:originRevision` variants examination 2
      accepted. Fix b2 (auxiliary media types, D.16.14) removes the `apv:mediaType` variants. On the re-imported
      500-run sample 61 of 877 shared keys still vary (as before b2): 45 judge files only in `apv:originPath`, 16 attempts
      only in `apv:artefactRole`; none in `apv:mediaType` (before: 16 in `apv:artefactRole` and `apv:mediaType`). The
      count is unchanged because every media variant came with a role variant. Datasheet item 16.
      - **Rejected:** moving `apv:originPath`/`apv:artefactRole` off the `raw:` entity to an execution-scoped node (a
        `prov/` change that alters the PROV of every corpus).
    - **Q2. Runs without an agent turn stay `verified_complete`.** In the sample, 6 of 498 agent executions (4 OpenClaw
      `direct_prompt` runs that log only the user step, 2 harness failures) have `dtap.acc.counters` as their only
      evaluated check, and it balances: 0 calls, 0 results. B2's rule (at least one evaluated check in an
      `agent_execution`) holds. Every run with an agent turn is `unverifiable`, because its model calls are derived.
      Datasheet item 14.
      - **Rejected:** requiring a core accounting check for `verified_complete` (an importer change for every family,
        for 6 runs whose counters do reconcile).
    - **Q3. At the full import, the corpus manifest records the pinned origin, never local staging paths.** The sample
      driver (`tools/dtap/import_dtap.py`) reads the staging worktrees through `LocalTree`, so `corpus.json` holds
      `{kind: local, path: "<home>/.agentprov/staging/..."}` beside the `runs` and `tasks` pins. The step-4 import must
      name the pins as the snapshot and context origins: through `agentprov import --verify-against-pin` once
      `raw/fetch.py` accepts Hugging Face dataset URLs (phase 12b item 4), or through an equivalent driver change.
      This is an AGENTS.md step-4 prerequisite.
      - **Rejected:** keeping the `<home>`-masked paths (the manifest would not name what the corpus was built from).
    - **Q4. Byte-identical judge-only files from different directories: one execution with two origins.** Identity stays
      content-addressed (D-27 c2, SEC-19; item 7 above). In the sample, the judge files of two judge-only directories
      of different tasks (`openaisdk/gpt-5.1/telecom/malicious/direct/privacy_leak_address/007` and
      `.../indirect/credential_leak/001`) are byte-identical. They give one `outcome_only` execution with two origins,
      whose task facets name the first directory; the second directory is a `dedup.collapsed` register row. So
      judge-only outcome units count distinct judge files, not directories. Per-directory counts remain possible from
      the origins (`raw/origins.jsonl`, the register). Rates are unaffected: `dtap.rate.outcome_only` excludes these
      units. Datasheet item 15.
      - **Rejected:** making the path part of a judge-primary unit's identity (it breaks content addressing for one
        kind of unit, and it is a mapper change for a count that the origins already give).
- **D-30 (2026-10-11, `derive` and `recompute` live in `corpus/`, reuse the T1 job kind `prov`, re-map through
  `import_source` and always write a new corpus; phase 11, implementation ruling).** The engine is
  `agentprov.corpus.derive` (L5) with `corpus/rawtree.py` and the CLI module `cli/derive.py`. It never imports
  `adapters.runner` or `adapters.registry`; what it needs from the adapter layer (`Catalogues.source_profile_sha256`,
  `Catalogues.semantics`) is injected by the CLI (M.5.2(1)).
  - **Never in place.** Both commands read `--corpus SRC` (sealed, working or `.partial`) through `CorpusReader` and write
    `NEW.partial` (`--out NEW`). `NEW` must not exist, must be disjoint from `SRC` and from every sealed corpus, and
    outside git. `--dry-run` builds into a private temporary tree that is removed afterwards, so it derives and compares
    exactly what `--out` would. Tests wrap every command in `testing.fs_guard.unchanged(SRC)`.
  - **Re-map and re-derive.** A re-map (`expand` or `aer` requested) feeds `StoredRawTree` (one candidate per non-member
    origin row, read from the source store with a digest check, the recorded origin, no network) to the public
    `adapters.runner.importer.import_source(..., until="aer")` with the values recorded in the source manifest and
    `derivation.json`. A re-derive copies the stored AER after re-verifying its seal. In both cases SEM, PROV and tiers
    3-4 then run as the existing job kind `prov` (by name, in batches over `WorkerPool`, consumed in index order); no job
    kind was added to `io/workers.py`.
  - **Pinned duplicates.** The `sem`/`prov`/`validation` stage definitions, `code_sha256` and the importer's `finish()`
    logic are re-implemented in `corpus/derive.py` (the B2 completeness rule is `corpus.facets.completeness_of`);
    `tests/unit/corpus/test_derive_definitions.py` pins them equal to the importer's.
  - **Comparison (H.8.4).** Per execution, by bytes and digests only (AER bytes and execution digest, SEM digest per
    profile, PROV file sha256 per spec, validation-row JCS digest, view bytes). A changed output is `changed_explained`
    when the declared identity of its stage or of a stage upstream differs between the two `derivation.json` files (the
    stage definition minus `fn_digest`, `engine_code_sha256`, `adapter_code_sha256` and the digests that sit beside an
    integer version, D-31); otherwise `unexplained_change` (exit 1). `failed`, `unverified`, a code-digest-only change
    that passes with a notice, `index_refreshed` and the corpus-level files (register, origins, members; HL-T14) are
    reported separately. `--show-diff N` prints the first differing line and the PROV semantic diff (`prov/diff.py`).
  - **Inputs first, resume.** Every listed raw object is re-hashed (`raw.digest.mismatch`) and the recorded
    catalogue/profile digests are compared with the package (`rules.mismatch`, `rules.unavailable`) before `NEW.partial`
    exists. The first file written is the working `corpus.json` with `derived_from` (`command`, `corpus_id`,
    `corpus_version|null`, `manifest_sha256`, `recomputed`, `root_digest|null`, `state`); a run with the same
    `derived_from` resumes, keyed on the sealed AER recorded in the index row (never on file existence); a different one
    is refused (exit 4).
  - **`derive` versus `recompute`.** `recompute` re-runs the requested stages (default: every stage the source has, from
    raw) and compares. `derive` adds missing layers (`sem,prov,validation`, `views`, `compat`) and carries present ones,
    refuses a requested present layer whose package definition has another declared identity (exit 4), and cannot
    re-map. `derive --trig DIR` writes TriG (E.5.4, `prov/serialise/trig.py`) with a `trig.sha256` listing.
  - **Reuse cache.** An execution's SEM, PROV and validation outputs are carried instead of recomputed when the reuse key
    is unchanged: same sealed AER, the same `fn_digest` of the three stage definitions, the same interpreter and core
    lockfile digest, the same digests for every catalogue and source profile the AER header declares, and every output
    present in the source row. The key is content-addressed only (no time, size or mtime). `--out` runs reuse by default,
    `--no-reuse` forces a full recompute and is the proof that a reusing run gave the same bytes (tested across `--jobs`
    1 and 4, re-derive and re-map); `recompute --dry-run` never reuses. The run is recorded in `derivation.json` as
    `reuse: {enabled, reused, recomputed, recomputed_executions}`. The key is coarse by design: a semantics-profile or
    catalogue change used by every execution recomputes every execution, because which executions a rule change affects
    cannot be known without recomputing them.
  - **Measured (derive-timings.md).** Zero unexplained differences on copies of the Mandate (396) and AgentHarm (1,056)
    p10 corpora; about 7-9 executions per second at 8-12 workers on a shared M2 Max; a re-map adds 10-25 % to a
    re-derive; tier-4 `pv.roundtrip` is 83-86 % of the cost (fixes proposed to the `validate/` owner, not applied).
  - **Why:** `corpus/` sits below `adapters.runner` (M.5.2); one pipeline (the job kind and `import_source` that import
    an execution also re-derive it) makes a recompute of an unchanged corpus byte-identical (Q.14) and lets an adapter fix
    be applied to an existing corpus without the network; never in place keeps every corpus immutable and a recompute
    transactional.
  - **Rejected:** `corpus.derive` importing `adapters.runner` or `adapters.profiles`; a new job kind `derive`; the
    baseline's in-place recompute; comparing parsed documents (`true`, `1`, `1.0`); counting a code-digest change as a
    version change (it would hide unintended output changes behind refactors); resuming on file existence (baseline R6);
    a finer per-rule reuse key (a wrong guess keeps stale provenance); reuse in `--dry-run`; a reuse key with
    timestamps or file sizes; threads or free-threaded Python for speed (worker processes are a security boundary).
