- **D-32 (2026-10-11, raw objects of `recompute --out` and `derive --out` are copied by default; `--link-raw` hard-links
  them; user-approved).** Each object is copied through `RawObjectStore.put_stream(..., expected_sha256=...)`, so it is
  re-hashed while it is copied. With `--link-raw` each object is hard-linked (`os.link`) from the source store, falling
  back to a copy with a notice when the file systems differ. `CorpusLayout.iter_tree` admits hard links and
  `testing.fs_guard` ignores `ctime` and the link count. This supersedes MN N.2.4(6) (link by default) for the default.
  - **Why:** a new version is released, moved and deposited independently of its source; a hard link ties the two trees
    to one inode. Linking is still available for large stores (the 2024-06 AgentDojo corpus).
  - **Rejected:** link by default; referencing the source store (the output would not be self-contained); copying
    without re-hashing (the inputs-first rule applies to the copy).
- **D-33 (2026-10-11, snapshot reconciliation and the sealed snapshot origin; phase 11).** (1) Counts in the sealed
  manifest are recomputed at sealing from `executions.jsonl`, `register.jsonl` and `raw/members.jsonl`, never copied from
  the importer. (2) A candidate is a selected execution-bearing file or member: `executions` = index rows whose
  `snapshot_ids` contain the snapshot, a selection exclusion is a `select`-stage `not_imported` entry whose path an
  exclude glob matches with the entry's own code (counted in `selection_excluded`, never a candidate), `not_imported` =
  every other `not_imported` entry attributed to the snapshot, `candidates = executions + not_imported`. This fixes
  AgentHarm (`candidates 6` against `executions 1056` becomes 1,056 = 1,056 + 0) and ROPE (14,066 exclusions become
  `selection_excluded`). (3) The sealed snapshot origin is built from the recorded pin and the objects' origins, never
  `local`: `git` `{repo, commit, subtree[, subtree_sha1]}`, `corpus` `{corpus, version, producer_commit}`; sealing refuses
  (exit 4) with no pin, `verification.unverified > 0`, a `local` object origin, a disagreement with the pin, or a spec
  origin that differs from the pin's. (4) A git origin has exactly one of `subtree` (a string, `""` for the whole commit)
  and `subtrees` (a sorted array of two or more relative paths; no v0.1 corpus uses it).
  - **Why:** H.2.3 requires `candidates == executions + not_imported` and the release refuses `local` origins; the
    working manifests break both. Counts defined from the register are recomputable by `verify --level chain`.
  - **Rejected:** copying the importer counters (they count containers); counting containers as candidates; a local path
    or placeholder origin in a sealed manifest (invariant 2); telling exclusions apart by the register `detail` text.
- **D-34 (2026-10-11, v0.1 index facets, generic cell, logical key, evidence classes and oracles; phase 11).** The v0.1
  facets are the H.3.3 core facets only (`task`, `framework`, `model.requested`, `model.served`, the eight `n.*` counts,
  `generic_types`, `outcome`); adapter facets (`x.<ns>.<name>`) and `--pipeline` are deferred (the row validator already
  accepts namespaced members). `corpus/facets.py` computes them as pure functions of the stored AER and SEM documents, so
  nothing comes from an adapter. Each facet and cell member carries the weakest effective evidence class of the fields it
  is computed from; `outcome` elements carry their own `ev`. The cell is generic (H.7.4): the recorded `task` members,
  `suite_set`, `model`, `attack_params_sha256`, `repeat`. A member the AER declares unknown is `{"$unk": reason}`, and
  `logical_key` is `null` iff a member is unknown (else `"lk_" + b32(sha256("aer-lk/1\n" + JCS(cell)))[:26]`, recomputed
  by the row validator). `oracles` has one entry per regression-oracle spec with output. Rows hold no floats
  (non-integral numbers are `{"$dec": ...}`, H.1.4(3)). A row is a working row (the importer's) or a full row with all
  five members and every stage; mixtures are rejected.
  - **Consequence (disclosed).** `logical_key` is `null` where the benchmark actor's `version` is unrecorded (all of
    `agentdojo-upstream-2024-06`, about two thirds of head, a few AgentDyn rows) and for every `adprov-v1-release` row;
    an adapter-declared cell that could supply an inferred suite set is deferred. An execution whose header leaves
    `instrumentation` unrecorded cannot show an attack parameter in its cell. No AER, SEM or PROV byte changes.
  - **Why:** H.3.3(3) requires facets re-derivable from AER and SEM and invariant 1 forbids adapters from defining
    them; the weakest-input rule never over-states an epistemic status.
  - **Rejected:** adapter-supplied facets and cells now (needs a declaration mechanism in the shared registry);
    strongest or majority class for `ev`; treating an unrecorded `instrumentation` as unknown attack parameters (imports
    that do not record it could then never have a key); floats as strings or rounded; judge or auxiliary models in
    `model.*`; failing a row whose key cannot be computed (H.7.4(3) says `null`).
- **D-35 (2026-10-11, two AgentDojo corpora from one profile; the corpus id comes from the corpus spec at sealing; user
  confirmed).** The June-2024 (`c274885`) and head (`089ed468`) working trees, which both record `corpus_id:
  agentdojo-upstream`, become two corpora, `agentdojo-upstream-2024-06` and `agentdojo-upstream-head` (D-27 c2), built
  from the one source profile `agentdojo-upstream@1`. The id is taken from the corpus spec at sealing
  (`corpora/<id>/corpus-spec.toml`), never from the working manifest. The two corpora deliberately share content-addressed
  execution ids (14,182 shared runs) and the datasheet says so (datasheet-items.md row 3). Checked read-only on 2026-10-11
  over every phase-10 working corpus (300 seeded-sample files each of AER, SEM and PROV): no corpus id appears in any
  AER/SEM/PROV byte, so renaming a corpus changes no byte and no golden digest.
  - **Why:** each snapshot is released, versioned and cited on its own, and the head tree's mixed generations do not
    enter the June-2024 corpus.
  - **Rejected:** one corpus with both snapshots (H.4.2's original layout); corpus-scoped execution ids; re-importing to
    change the working manifests' `corpus_id` (PLAN rule 3).
- **D-36 (2026-10-11, the claims and lint library is a new file `adapters/registry/claims.py`; user-approved).** The one
  claims/lint library of I.5.6, H.9(4) and N.2.5(7) holds the closed claim-tag vocabulary and the tagged must-not-claim
  items, the registry-generated coverage phrase, the registered datasheet claims, and the text, card and datasheet
  lints; `CHECKER` is injected into `corpus.datasheet.render` by its caller (`cli.package`), so `corpus/` (L5) never
  imports it. `validate --card` calls `lint_card` from the CLI. Card allow-list (H.9(3)) as built: version ids, SemVer,
  ISO dates and year-months, DOIs, arXiv ids, commit SHAs, section and item numbers, rule and profile references and
  identifiers in code spans are allowed; every other number is a placeholder (`{{v:}}`, `{{t:}}`, `{{claim:}}`, and in a
  decided statement `{{f:}}`).
  - **Why:** AD-10 row 9 merges the claims registry and the card linter into one library that also serves the README,
    the paper and `stats`; a new file keeps the existing registry modules untouched (append-only rule).
  - **Rejected:** a claims module under `corpus/` (an L5 to L6 import) or a second card linter; detecting must-not-claim
    tags in free prose by keyword.
- **D-37 (2026-10-11, compat outputs through `derive --prov-spec adprov-v2.3-compat`; user ruling: the released adprov-v1
  carries the compat graphs, no other corpus does).** The transcript/v1 view of each AER is built in the parent, run
  through the frozen oracle (`CompatSpec.build`) and stored at `prov/adprov-v2.3-compat/<ss>/<ex>.prov.json`; for every
  other adapter the stage is `not_applicable`. `agentprov.prov.specs.load_compat_spec()` is the only importer of
  `prov.compat` outside `migration` and tests (M.5.2(3)), and only when requested. Each row with compat output has
  `oracles: {"adprov-v2.3-compat": {"gate_report": null, "status": "apv:RegressionOracle"}}`; the working manifest has
  `prov_specs` and `oracle_specs` (`[]` when none). The CLI prints the oracle's `NOTICE` (R-55, Q.30) on stderr and in the
  summary's `notices`. `derivation.json` gets separate `views` and `compat` stage entries, so the importer's resume check
  is unaffected. `recompute` re-derives and compares existing compat output; it cannot add it.
  - **Why:** the compat graphs are the regression oracle of the migration (gate B); an explicit, flagged layer of a new
    version keeps them out of the default derivation and stops a reader mistaking them for the recommended semantics.
  - **Rejected:** compat during `import`; compat inside the T1 `prov` job (it would load the quarantined package in every
    worker); importing `prov.compat` from `corpus/`; compat for every AgentDojo-family corpus.
- **D-38 (2026-10-11, deposit verification: inputs and archive mode without extraction; phase 11).** `agentprov verify
  --corpus PATH` picks its mode from PATH without following a link: a directory holding `DEPOSIT-MANIFEST.json` is a
  deposit, a `<id>-v<ver>.meta.zip` is a lone meta archive, anything else a corpus tree (N.1.5). Archives are opened
  only through `agentprov.ingest.archives` (the G.3.5 gate) and members are streamed and hashed in memory; nothing is
  extracted. Member names are labels: they carry the corpus prefix `<id>-v<ver>/` and the H.1.2 grammar, and a label in
  two archives trusts neither. The union of a corpus's archives is the closed world of its own `checksums.sha256` (the
  archive-mode `ChecksumSource`); the deposit manifest (sizes, sha256, md5, `n_members`, `uncompressed_bytes`,
  `members_sha256`, root and content digests) is checked against it, never trusted for it. Levels: `chain` (default)
  runs unchanged over an archive-backed reader, `checksums` is available, `rederive` exits 5 (it needs a raw store on
  disk). A lone meta archive is checked against its own checksums and reports the rest `unverified`, never passed
  (`--release` fails it). Archive reading runs in the CLI process with the ingest limits (member bound raised to the
  deposit format's no-ZIP64 bound); a T1 `verify` job kind is a phase-12 follow-up. The deposit builder injects
  `verify --level chain`; `seal()` runs it too before the swap (N.2.11 step 3); `validate --corpus` stays read-only on
  working corpora (a departure from N.2.5(4): `derive` is the writer of the validation stage). Details:
  `docs/reports/phase11/decisions/D-38.md`.
  - **Why:** H.10.3(1) and G.3.5 forbid extraction; the corpus's own checksums and the published root digest are the
    authority, the deposit manifest is a claim to check.
  - **Rejected:** extracting to a temporary tree; a new T1 job kind now (`io/workers.py`/`worker.py` are phase 12's);
    trusting `DEPOSIT-MANIFEST.json` for the closed world; failing a lone meta archive outright; `rederive` by streaming
    raw members into a scratch store (extraction by another name).
- **D-39 (2026-10-11, `verify --root-digest sha256:…`; phase 11).** The option (repeatable) takes a root digest
  published outside the corpus (tag annotation, paper, deposit record) and compares it with
  `"sha256:" + sha256(checksums.sha256)` (H.5.4) at every level; in archive mode each digest must equal one corpus's.
  A difference is `root_digest.mismatch` (exit 1); a working tree cannot match (`root_digest.unverifiable`). `verify
  --release` in tree mode or on a lone meta archive requires it (exit 2 otherwise); a deposit is anchored by its
  manifest, where the option stays the only defence against an end-to-end consistent forgery. **Amended by D-620
  (2026-10-22):** a deposit manifest anchors nothing, so `verify --release` on a deposit directory requires it too.
  The computed root digest is printed after every run and never written into the corpus. Details:
  `docs/reports/phase11/decisions/D-39.md`.
  - **Why:** a regenerated `checksums.sha256` over files no digest chain covers (`DATASHEET.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
    `LICENSES/**`) is detected only by a digest kept outside the tree (K.12.5).
  - **Rejected:** reading the expected digest from inside the corpus or deposit (circular); requiring it in dev mode;
    bare hex digests; treating a mismatch as `unverified`.
- **D-40 (2026-10-11, the corpus `ValidationSummary`: mode, per-check version and tier, tier results,
  `linkage_resolved_pct`; phase 11).** `corpus.json.validation` is computed at sealing from `validation/summary.json`,
  `validation/results.jsonl` and the `validation` stage of `derivation.json`: `mode` (`strict` when the stage ran in
  release mode; `package` refuses anything else), `checks` (`id`, `version`, `tier`, counts), `tiers` (per tier: checks,
  summed results, `executions`, `executions_passed`), `linkage` (`applicable`, `resolved` over the `pv.linkage.*`
  checks), `linkage_resolved_pct` and `libraries`. `linkage_resolved_pct = floor(10000 * resolved / applicable) / 100`
  written as the decimal `{"$dec": "100.00"}`, `null` when `applicable == 0`; the phase-10 corpora give `100.00`.
  - **Why:** the paper's claim `c1-linkage` and its validation table are read from the sealed corpus, not recomputed by
    the paper pipeline; floats are forbidden in the corpus layer (H.1.4(3)).
  - **Rejected:** a float percentage; rounding to nearest (99.996 % would read as 100.00); counting check results
    instead of executions.
- **D-41 (2026-10-11, `sources[].lineage` is the profile's `[lineage]` table verbatim; the `duplicates` summary shape;
  phase 11).** The manifest records the declaration the build used, copied verbatim (R-45, H.7.3, Q.29); `sources[].mirrors`
  is `[]` in v0.1 (mirrors are `[lineage].duplicates` entries with `relation = "mirror"`). `duplicates` holds computed
  tallies only: `{content_dedup: "never", collapsed, multi_origin_executions, multi_snapshot_executions,
  owned_elsewhere}`, which `verify --level chain` can recompute from the index and the register.
  - **Why:** converting `[lineage]` into H.2.3's `LineageDecl` would invent `basis` and `ev` values the profiles do not
    record (invariant 2).
  - **Rejected:** that conversion; repeating declared duplicates in `duplicates`; content-based duplicate counts
    (fingerprint deduplication is deferred, AD-10 row 7).
- **D-42 (2026-10-11, licence classes in deposits; the offline deposit builder and its archive format; phase 11;
  includes the release-scan rulings of the user).**
  - **Classes.** The class of a sealed corpus is `(licences.derived.spdx, sorted licences.restrictions)`, checked equal to
    the recorded `licences.class`. SPDX ids compare exactly (`GPL-3.0-only`, `GPL-3.0-or-later`, `AGPL-3.0-only` are three
    classes, D-25), and two corpora whose restrictions differ in any clause are two classes (`ast-survey-agentharm`).
  - **Refusals (exit 4).** Corpora of different classes in one deposit (`release.refused.mixed_licence_classes`) unless
    `--allow-mixed-licence-classes`, recorded in `deposit-metadata.json`, `DEPOSIT-MANIFEST.json` and a deposit note in
    each datasheet copy (the sealed corpus is never modified); a non-commercial class outside a corpus whose id ends `-nc`
    with policy `nc_partition` (an `-nc` class is never mixed, even with the override); relicensing a GPL/AGPL/LGPL or
    non-commercial source; raw policy `withhold`, licence policy `forbidden` or redistribution `not-permitted`; an
    unsealed, working or `.partial` tree; non-strict validation; an `interpreter_advisory` corpus; no release scan for the
    same root digest or an untriaged or `real` finding unless `WITHHELD.json` names its fingerprint (no scan result is a
    refusal, never a skip). Release mode below CPython 3.14.8 exits 3. A corpus with a `views/` tree exits 5 (views are
    not deposited in v0.1, AD-10 row 12).
  - **Offline by construction.** `agentprov.release` imports no network or process module and calls nothing named upload
    or publish (static, dynamic and behaviour tests). The scan, the verifier and the claims lint are injected
    (`scan=`, `verify=`, `lint=`). gitleaks 8.30.1 runs in `tools/release_scan.py` (`dir --redact
    --ignore-gitleaks-allow`, explicit default-rules config, reduced environment), so nothing inside scanned data can
    change the rules or hide a finding; no matched value is recorded; triage comes from a reviewed TOML file per
    fingerprint and per sealed root digest (`agentprov-release-scan/0.1`).
  - **Archive format** (the contract for archive-mode `verify`, D-38). `<id>-v<ver>.meta.zip` and
    `<id>-v<ver>.<stage>.<nnn>.zip` (stage `raw`, `aer`, `sem-<profile_dir>`, `prov-<spec_dir>`); regular files only,
    sorted bytewise, fixed `date_time` (release date, clamped to 1980-01-01), `create_system = 3`, `external_attr =
    0o100644 << 16`, DEFLATE level 6, no extra field, comment or data descriptor, no ZIP64 (below 2^31 − 1 bytes and
    65,535 members). Splitting is on shard boundaries on a deterministic upper bound of each member's stored size, so
    membership depends only on the corpus, never on the zlib version. Each member is re-hashed while written.
    `DEPOSIT-MANIFEST.json` (`agentprov-deposit-manifest/0.1`) and `deposit-metadata.json` (`agentprov-deposit/0.1`,
    `status: draft-unpublished`, `version_doi` always null, `concept_doi` and related identifiers only from `release.toml`
    and the sealed corpus) are written; nothing is uploaded or published. Two builds from the same inputs are
    byte-identical (Q.20), including from two independent copies of a seal.
  - **Release-scan rulings (user, 2026-10-11).** AgentPROV's own content-addressed keys (`derivationKey`, `subject_key`,
    `logical_key`) are known false positives: one committed allowlist (`_KEY_ALLOWLIST`) matches only the anchored
    `key":"(ex_|lk_)?<26 base32>"` text, so a secret elsewhere in the same JSONL record is still reported. AgentHarm's
    credential-shaped strings are fake benchmark values: the findings inside the AgentHarm content of
    `ast-survey-agentharm` (114 in the rehearsal) are triaged `synthetic-benchmark`, still per fingerprint and per root
    digest; home-path and host-name findings are not covered.
  - **Rehearsal** (`docs/reports/phase11/deposit-rehearsal.md`, on copies): Mandate sealed in 6.5 s (396 executions, 1,616
    files) and AgentHarm in 22.5 s (1,056, 4,262); each deposit built twice byte-identical (9.1 MB and 54.0 MB of
    archives); a Mandate plus AgentHarm deposit exited 4 and wrote nothing.
  - **Why:** the licence class is what decides whether corpora can share a deposit and a concept DOI; a draft that cannot
    publish and cannot reach the network keeps the release a human act (D-5).
  - **Rejected:** letting the override mix an `-nc` class (H.4.2 requires a separate deposit); splitting on actual
    compressed sizes (membership would depend on zlib); ZIP64 for the `2**31` default (H.10.4 forbids extra fields);
    running gitleaks from the builder (H.10.1 requires it offline with no subprocess); skipping a missing scan or
    verification silently; per-corpus triage of the generated keys (thousands per corpus); a line-level allowlist (a JSONL
    record is one line); copying `release-scan.json` into the deposit.
  - **Deferred:** `verify --level chain` before archiving and archive-mode `verify` of the deposit (D-38; U4 supplies
    them through `verify=`); a `synthetic` marker; separate concept DOIs per class (H.10.6).
  - **Allowlist widened for fragment cuts (2026-10-12).** gitleaks scans long lines in fragments, so a match can be
    cut at a fragment boundary (U4 rehearsal: `ivationKey":"…"`, a key without its closing quote). The allowlist
    accepts a field name cut at the start down to six characters and a key cut at the end down to 16 characters, and
    nothing else (never another full field name such as `activationKey` or `project_key`); 0 findings remain on the
    Mandate corpus.
- **D-43 (2026-10-11, live corpora cannot be re-mapped; their SEM/PROV/validation re-derive; phase 11).** For a corpus with
  `"mode": "live"`, `recompute` with `expand` or `aer` among its `--stages` exits 5 (unsupported) before anything beyond
  the manifest and index is read, naming the alternative. Without `--stages`, a live corpus starts from the stored AERs.
  `recompute --stages sem,prov,validation` (and `views`, `compat`) and `derive` work as for imports.
  - **Why:** a live AER is mapped from capture logs by the session pipeline (`adapters/runner/session.py`), not by
    `import_source`; a second live re-map path is outside phase 11's ownership.
  - **Rejected:** re-mapping capture logs through `import_source` (it would silently produce different AERs); exit 2
    (the request is well formed; the capability is missing, N.1.3); silently skipping the AER stage.
- **D-44 (2026-10-11, corpus specs in git; the eight v0.1 corpus directories; derived licence `inherit`; user rulings).**
  - `.gitignore`: `/corpora/` becomes M.3.1's `/corpora/*/*` with negations for `corpus-spec.toml`, `CARD.md` and
    `CHANGES.toml`; the decided statements table `corpora/datasheet-statements.toml` is committed too. The eight corpora
    (`adprov-v1-release`, `agentdojo-upstream-2024-06`, `agentdojo-upstream-head`, `rope`, `agentdyn-a`,
    `mandate-agentdojo-eval`, `ast-survey-agentdojo`, `ast-survey-agentharm`) each get a spec (H.1.6), a card (H.9) and a
    `0.1.0` changelog entry; the snapshot origin is the pin the phase-10 import recorded (D-33), checked against the
    in-package profile pins.
  - **User ruling:** the derived licence is `inherit` for every corpus (MIT for AgentDojo, ROPE, AgentDyn and Mandate;
    CC-BY-4.0 for the survey corpora and the AgentDojo-PROV release). Licence facts are read at sealing from the source
    profile's `[licence]` table, never typed into a spec.
  - **User ruling:** `ast-survey-agentharm` is its own restricted-use class, `(CC-BY-4.0, [the AgentHarm use clause])`,
    distinct from `ast-survey-agentdojo`'s `(CC-BY-4.0, [])`.
  - **User ruling:** the `adprov-v1-release` `LICENSE` is the CC-BY-4.0 legal code (the release's data stamp), and the
    embedded AgentDojo MIT notice is `AgentDojo-LICENSE`; the agentdojo-prov repository `LICENSE` (MIT, code) is not shipped.
  - `[licence] files` (an as-built addition to H.1.6) names the verbatim upstream files written to `LICENSES/<source_id>/`;
    `package` takes each from the corpus's own raw store when the import stored it at the pinned commit (Mandate's
    `LICENSE`), otherwise from `--licence-file NAME=PATH`, and records the provenance in the generated `NOTICE.md`.
  - **Open items (marked TODO in the specs):** the upstream `LICENSE` (and AgentDojo's `CITATION.bib`) of AgentDojo, ROPE,
    AgentDyn and the survey are not in their raw stores (the imports select `runs/` or a subtree) and are supplied at
    sealing; the DTap-Bench corpus id is not fixed.
  - **Why:** H.1.6 puts the build inputs under version control next to the code, and M.3.1's negations keep corpora out
    of git (invariant 6); inheriting the source licence avoids any relicensing question (U-03).
  - **Rejected:** committing the whole `corpora/` tree or licence texts under `corpora/<id>/`; copying licence facts into
    the specs; a separate licence decision per corpus.
- **D-45 (2026-10-11, `render` is on demand only; `--all` is removed and `--select` needs `--limit`; phase 11, user rule).**
  `agentprov render` has no `--all`; a bare `render --corpus DIR` is a usage error (exit 2). Allowed selections are
  `--ex ID...`, `--limit N`, and `--select KEY=VALUE[,VALUE...]` together with `--limit N` (a filter alone can match every
  execution). Output location and guard, `--bundle`, `--format`, `--show-content`, `--jobs`, `--dry-run` and determinism
  are unchanged.
  - **Why:** with 18,000 to 35,000 executions per corpus and one Graphviz process per graph, a render-all is a job of
    hours that nobody means to start from a shell; removing the option makes the safe behaviour the only one.
  - **Rejected:** `--all` behind a confirmation flag; requiring `--limit` for `--ex` (a typed list is already finite); a
    hard cap on `--limit`; `--select` alone with a warning.
- **D-46 (2026-10-11, `purge` lives in `corpus/purge.py` and `cli/purge.py`, not `raw/purge.py`; phase 11).** MN M.1.2 and
  G.9.6 name `agentprov.raw.purge`, but `raw/` belongs to phase 12; the engine uses the public read API of `raw` and the
  tombstone path `CorpusLayout.tombstones` (moving it later is a rename). A purge targets a working corpus (`--corpus DIR`,
  acting on `DIR.partial`) or the fetch cache (`--cache`, `--cache-dir`). It writes one tombstone row `{date, reason,
  sha256}` (sorted by digest, no value), gives every citing execution (and, for a container, its members' executions)
  `release.withheld`, then unlinks the object, so an interrupted purge is finished by running it again; origin rows, member
  rows and the index are kept. A sealed corpus is refused (exit 4); a non-interactive run needs `--yes`, a terminal asks
  for the first 8 digits. Purging a container lists the stored member objects, and vice versa; it never removes more than
  the one object asked for. `corpus.json` counts and index `issues` are not rewritten (derive and seal refresh them).
  - **Why:** the tombstone, `release.withheld` and the confirmation fit the corpus layer, which owns the register and the
    file layout; tombstone first and unlink last makes the operation resumable without a journal.
  - **Rejected:** editing `raw/`; waiting for phase 12 (phase 11 ships all fifteen commands); rewriting
    `executions.jsonl` and `corpus.json` in the purge (a second writer invites drift, D-33); withholding only exact-digest
    citations; automatic cascades; searching git objects in the cache.
  - **Open (phase 12):** a later `import` into the same working corpus would store a tombstoned file again; blocking
    tombstoned digests at ingest is raw-layer work.
- **D-47 (2026-10-11, the SEC-07 calibration, the obs-G8 reproduction and expand streaming move to phase 12; user-approved).**
  The PQ row-11 exit items on SEC-07 live in `raw/`, `io/workers.py`/`worker.py` and `tests/security/`, which phase 12
  owns: (1) calibrating the provisional expand-job CPU and wall budgets of G.4.3 with the SEC-07 case of more than 256 MiB
  of selected members (G.11.3 open question 13; a synthetic seeded archive generated at test time plus the cached survey
  `artifact.zip`, no download); (2) an exact obs-G8 reproduction showing that the post-open ZIP prefix check
  (`ingest.archive.prefix`, G.3.5) rejects the archive; (3) streaming `expand` instead of reading the whole container into
  memory (`raw/members.py`, HL.R7). The budgets stay provisional until then.
  - **Why:** phase 11 must not edit those files (ownership rules); the items test code phase 12 changes.
  - **Rejected:** doing them in phase 11 behind the ownership rule; dropping them.
- **D-48 (2026-10-11, `agentprov stats` and `agentprov.api` design choices; phase 11).**
  - **One streamed pass per corpus, never pooled.** `stats.compute(corpora, tables)` opens each corpus with `CorpusReader`
    (read-only), streams the index once and reads an AER or PROV file only when a table needs it. Single process (N.2.12
    asks for no `--jobs`). An unreadable file is a counted per-execution failure (exit 1), never a silent skip; output
    carries no path and no clock. A sealed corpus runs the H.5.5 `checksums` level (a failing corpus gets no tables and
    exits 1); a working tree is `verification: "not_sealed"` with a notice. The report carries `fn_digest` and
    `field_groups_sha256`. The grouping key is `(source_id, profile)`: counts may be aggregated, rates never (O.3.5).
  - **Tables.** `counts` (status, unit, `execution_observed`, completeness, `n_executions` = agent executions observed,
    `n_outcome_only`, PROV output, rate exclusions, registry parts and import status, register entries); `statements`
    recounted from the stored PROV-JSON (an entry carrying `apv:evidenceClass`; bundle kinds from the E.4.2 bundle IRI;
    unclassified entries in `statements_structural`; an unknown rule is counted and a failure; `--per-execution` adds the
    O.3.5 frame, which sums to the aggregate); `unknowns` per occurrence source; `field_groups` from
    `stats/field_groups.toml`, the data form of C.3.16 (coverage `(O + D) / (cells − not_applicable)`, observed share, an
    `undeclared` count for absences without an `unk`, `message_roles` mapping `agent` to `assistant` as data).
  - **Rate exclusions are family data, never code** (D.16.17 item 4): read from `adapters/<family>/rates.toml` as package
    data without importing an adapter module; `stats` holds no source name (a test scans for every registered source id).
    No family ships one yet (DTap adds its own).
  - **Output.** JSON (JCS + LF, schema-checked in tests), text, Markdown, CSV (formula guard); data-derived labels pass
    `escape_untrusted`. `--corpus` repeatable, `--tables`, `--artefacts` (`agentprov.artefacts.scan` per execution),
    `--per-execution`, `--prov-spec`, `--select`, `--format`, `--out` (atomic, refused inside any corpus, G8).
  - **`agentprov.api`** (M.6) re-exports the stats objects; deviations are in its docstring (`read_aer(row, corpus=...)`,
    `rows(corpus, "lineage")`, `check_claim`, `coverage_phrase` and `lint_text` delegating to the claims library, D-36).
  - **Smoke** (`docs/reports/phase11/stats-smoke.md`): AgentHarm (1,056) 15.9 s base and 18.7 s with `--artefacts
    --per-execution`; Mandate (396) 3.7 s and 5.1 s; outputs byte-identical across runs; the working corpora unchanged
    (`fs_guard`).
  - **Why:** recounting from stored files is what K.5.11 item 2 asks for (an independent recount); the weakest-input and
    declared/undeclared distinctions keep the information-loss figure honest.
  - **Rejected:** reading the engine's report (not stored in a corpus); hard-coded exclusions; extending the artefact or
    rule catalogue schema with exclusion keys (owned elsewhere); counting executions without a cell in the coverage
    denominator; pooling across corpora or profiles; `--jobs`.
- **D-49 (2026-10-11, gate D at full scope validates stored AERs, read-only, in a plain process pool; phase 11).**
  `agentprov migrate gate-d [--scope golden|full] [--release] [--workers N] [--corpus DIR ...] [--limit N]
  [--accept-gap TREE ...] [--report PATH]` (also `migrate gate D`). `golden` derives the 19 v1 and 9 native golden AERs
  twice and checks the committed pins; `full` reads the AERs of `--corpus DIR` (once per tree: `release`, `converted`,
  `native`, classified from the index rows) through `CorpusReader` and never writes into a corpus (a `--report` inside a
  corpus is refused, exit 4). Per execution it runs tiers 2-4 in release mode (a failed or skipped check fails the
  execution, MP-3) plus the dedicated J.3.5 checks; per tree it compares the aggregates with the J.3.5 table and the
  completeness 17,664 / 18,027 / 18,241. Full scope without `--limit` needs passing full-scope G0, A and B reports for the
  commit and lock, and its own passing report unblocks a full-scope gate E; `--limit N` is a diagnostic sample. A tree
  without a corpus fails `inputs.<tree>.present` unless `--accept-gap TREE` is given, and the report then records the gap.
  - **Finding:** no stored AERs of the converted tree exist (gates A and B map the converted transcripts into a temporary
    directory and delete them), so a full run needs `--accept-gap converted` and the native corpus's 18,027 matched
    executions are checked against that column. The AER side of the J.3.5 table reconciles exactly on the stored AERs.
  - **Measured:** about 0.96 s per execution on a 200-execution slice (tier 4 is about 90 %), so roughly one hour at ten
    workers for 35,905 executions. Not run in phase 11.
  - **Why a plain process pool, not the T1 job kind `prov`:** the job cannot carry `migration=True`, returns no derivation
    report (the J.3.5 counts would be re-parsed from 7,000-statement documents in the parent), needs a job kind in
    `io/workers.py` (phase 12) and a scratch write per execution. The inputs were validated and sealed at import and are
    re-verified before use. The report states `isolation.mode: process-pool, grade: null`.
  - **Rejected:** re-mapping the converted tree inside gate D (a producer step, not a validation of existing AERs); treating
    the missing tree as `skipped` (a skipped check is a failure) or failing forever (gate E full could never run);
    using the converted column for the 7 Mixtral and 207 empty logs; a default report path below `docs/reports/migration/`.
- **D-50 (2026-10-11, phase 12a: the tier-2 AER validator and the locator resolver never raise on parsed input).** AER
  read back from a corpus or a deposit is untrusted (G.1.3). Every check of `aer.validate` treats a type-confused field
  (a scalar where a list belongs, an unhashable value where a code or reason belongs, a non-string pointer, a pointer
  token longer than any index) as a finding of its own or as unresolvable, never as an exception; `pointer_get` refuses
  non-strings and over-long array indices before `int()`. Found by the phase-12a fuzz layer and the coverage audit
  (`docs/reports/hardening/sec-coverage.md` §5.2); valid AER validates exactly as before, so no corpus byte changes.
  - **Rejected:** wrapping the validator in one `try/except` (it would hide which check failed and stop the remaining
    checks); relying on the structural schema pass alone (the semantic passes still run on the same record).
- **D-51 (2026-10-11, phase 12a: the fuzz layer lives in `tests/fuzz/` with per-suite budgets, not global Hypothesis
  profiles).** K.11.1's `ci` and `thorough` profiles are budgets in `tests/fuzz/fuzz_support.py`, selected by
  `AGENTPROV_FUZZ=thorough` (×20 examples, not derandomised); the `ci` budgets run in `core` on every push and pull
  request, the thorough ones only in the dispatch-only CI job `fuzz-thorough`. Each fuzz module runs in an empty working
  directory that must stay empty (F-3). Seeds are the committed fixtures, read by the tests and never printed.
  - **Rejected:** `settings.load_profile` in a conftest (it changes every other suite's Hypothesis settings); a
    scheduled fuzz job (D-22); atheris (deferred, AD-10 row 18).
- **D-52 (2026-10-11, phase 12a: shipped archive-selection globs are pinned linear by test; the compiler is hardened
  only with the regeneration).** `raw.members` keeps `glob.translate` semantics (a `*` stays in its segment). A segment
  with several `*` separated by literals backtracks super-linearly (80 s on a 200-character label), but no shipped
  profile has that shape, and `tests/security/test_selection_patterns.py` keeps it so. Refusing such patterns in
  `Selection` is recorded in the regeneration batch, because `raw/members.py` is an `EXPAND_MODULES` file and any edit
  changes the `expand` stage's `fn_digest`.
  - **Rejected:** switching to `fnmatch` (its `*` crosses `/`, a selection change); hardening now (a `fn_digest` change
    between a paused import and its resume makes the resume refuse, AGENTS.md §0).
- **D-53 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: Hugging Face dataset repositories are git pins with their own cache namespace).**
  `raw/fetch.py` `_split_repo` returns `(host, namespace, repo)`. On `huggingface.co` exactly
  `https://huggingface.co/datasets/<owner>/<name>[.git]` is accepted, with namespace `("datasets", <owner>)`, so the
  depth-1 cache is `git/huggingface.co/datasets/<owner>/<name>.git` and the history store and index follow the same path
  (D.16.18 item 13; MN N.1.11 item 5). Every other host keeps the one shape `https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>`.
  - **Why:** the DTap `runs` and `tasks` pins are Hugging Face dataset repositories; without this they could not be
    fetched, seeded or used by `--verify-against-pin`, and `fetch --references` raised on loading the `dtap-bench` profile.
  - **Refused on `huggingface.co`:** `spaces/`, `models/`, a dataset path with fewer or more parts, and a two-part path
    whose owner is `datasets`, `models` or `spaces` (case-insensitive): a model repository `datasets/<x>` would otherwise
    sit beside the dataset directories in the cache.
  - **Rejected:** a host-independent three-part shape (it would admit arbitrary nesting on every host); keying the cache
    by a hash of the URL (the readable layout of N.1.11 item 5 is relied on by the seeding tools and the reports).
  - **Effect:** no AER, SEM or PROV byte changes; `fetch.py` is not an `expand` module, so no `fn_digest` moves.
- **D-54 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: no git call of the fetch layer may fetch lazily; absent blobs are a typed refusal;
  routing R2).** `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` is part of the Fetcher's fixed git environment, so it applies to every call (the
  depth-1 store, the history store, the seeding tool's file-protocol fetch). `parse_ls_tree` refuses a tree in which any
  entry's size is `BAD` with `AbsentBlobError` (`raw.fetch.blob_absent`, carrying the absent paths as labels), and any
  other non-decimal size with `raw.fetch.git`; before, `int("BAD")` raised `ValueError`. `tools/seed_git_cache.py`
  prints the code (with a hint when the clone's config names a promisor remote) and exits with its status.
  - **Why / what was measured:** git ≥ 2.45.1 already disables lazy fetching inside `upload-pack` by default, so the
    routed case (seeding from a `blob:none` clone over the file protocol) failed without network use on git 2.54.0; but
    `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=0` turns it back on, and **local reads** were not covered: `ls-tree -l` on a depth-1 store with a
    promisor remote fetched every absent blob from that remote (reproduced offline with a local upstream;
    `tests/unit/raw/test_fetch.py::test_without_the_guard_reading_a_partial_store_fetches_from_its_upstream`).
  - **Rejected:** refusing every partial clone up front (the phase-10d trial seeds from partial clones whose absent
    blobs lie outside the pinned paths); skipping absent entries (a half-read tree would pass expectations silently).
  - **Effect:** no AER, SEM or PROV byte changes; `fetch.py` is not an `expand` module.
- **D-55 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: a declared, bounded memory cap per job kind; `prov` gets 4 GiB; user decision).**
  `io/workers.py` declares `KIND_RSS_BYTES = {"prov": 4 GiB}`; `WorkerLimits.kind_rss_bytes` carries it and every cap
  (default, per kind) is validated into [64 MiB, 16 GiB]. A job runs under the cap of its kind
  (`WorkerLimits.for_kind`). The default worker count uses the largest cap (`max_rss_bytes`; user choice (a)); a
  defaulted Linux `RLIMIT_AS` is `max(4 GiB, largest cap + 1 GiB)`, an explicit one is kept. The pool's isolation
  record names the caps (`memory_caps`). G.4.3.
  - **Why:** the 2 GiB cap is sized for parsing untrusted bytes (64 MiB × 24); a `prov` job reads a sealed AER and its
    memory grows with run length in tier 4. Measured in real workers on 14 DTap runs chosen by steps, size and the LFS
    objects (`docs/reports/hardening/prov-rss.md`): 0.6–1.4 GiB up to 17 MB of PROV, 1.9–2.5 GiB at 24–30 MB (four runs
    the 2 GiB cap kills), about 80–90 MiB per MB of PROV. 4 GiB covers every measured run that completes today.
  - **User decisions (2026-10-12):** default 4 GiB, ceiling 16 GiB, worker count from the largest cap; a recorded
    per-run override up to the ceiling (CLI flag and its record in the corpus producer block are routed to the
    orchestrator: `cli/` and the importer/`derive` are not phase 12b's).
  - **Not solved by a cap:** PROV-JSON over 64 MiB fails tier 4 at parse (`pv.prov_structure.not_json`; the validator
    loads it with the default `max_json_bytes`), and one over 256 MiB exceeds the per-member output cap
    (`worker.limit.output`; DTap `pii-4`, 1,557 steps). Both are routed (validator owner) with the measurements.
  - **Rejected:** one larger cap for every kind (weakens the containment of parsers); counting workers from the 2 GiB
    default (12 × 4 GiB can exceed a 32 GB host); an unbounded or RAM-relative cap (not declared, host-dependent output).
  - **Effect:** no output byte changes; which executions are registered `worker.limit.rss` changes (fewer).
- **D-56 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: D-91 implemented: `:` is a label character inside an archive member component).**
  `ingest/names.py` drops `:` from the Windows-invalid set; in portable mode a component that starts with
  `[A-Za-z]:` is a traversal form in every position (before, only the whole name's first two characters were checked).
  The expand job emits one info finding `ingest.name.colon` per container with the count of such labels (new code in the
  closed G.3.9 registry, so the register accepts it with no `corpus/` change); the parent now keeps a finding's

  existing output changes). G.3.6, G.3.9.
  - **Check required by D-91 (done):** no layout, register or deposit path is built from a member label. Raw objects
    are `raw/objects/<sha[:2]>/<sha>.<ext>` with `ext` from the closed table of `raw.store.ext_for_label`; register
    subjects are `{snapshot_id, path}` JSON values and the `rid` is over their JCS; `subject_key`
    (`snapshot_id:path`) is a sort key that is recomputed and compared, never split (a `snapshot_id` already contains
    `:` for context roles, `importer.py`); the deposit builder names corpus files, whose names follow the H.1.3
    grammar. The importer's context references `"<role>:<label>"` split at the first `:` and `role` has no `:`.
  - **Rejected:** allowing a drive-form component after the first (`a/C:x`): nothing would break today, but D-91 keeps
    the drive-letter check and a label may yet be shown to a Windows user as a path.
  - **Effect:** `ingest/names.py`, `ingest/errors` registry (`errors.py`) and `raw/members.py` are `EXPAND_MODULES`: the
    `expand` `fn_digest` moves (bundled with C3, user decision 2026-10-12; regen-batch.md). Members that were rejected
    `ingest.name.invalid` for `:` alone are selected at the next import; no AER/SEM/PROV byte of an existing corpus
    changes (Figshare 32657856 is not imported).
- **D-57 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: D-90 implemented: a bounded framing reader for a gzip tar nested in a zip; user
  approval of the written recommendation `docs/reports/hardening/d90-recommendation.md`).** `ingest/streams.py`
  `iter_gzip_bounded` and `ingest/archives.py` `OpenedTar` (own 512-byte header parser, two passes, no `tarfile`),
  reached through `open_archive` at depth ≥ 2 only; tar members get `member` origins with `method` 0 and a streamed
  CRC-32 (C.3.12 note). Spec G.3.5 "As built".
  - **Why:** 22,397 runs (Zenodo 22011266 and 22973265's version 23138310) are the only ones in the candidate set with
    GPT-6 Luna/Sol, gpt-5.4(-mini) and claude-sonnet-4-6 under AgentDojo defences; the staged deposit uses 3,219 GNU
    long-name headers, the obs-G1 type that `tarfile` buffers unbounded.
  - **Rejected:** `tarfile` behind a pre-scan (the buffering is inside `tarfile.next()`); an intermediate stored `.tar`
    object (duplicates up to `max_total_bytes`, and `aer/0.1` has no origin kind for it); top-level `tar.gz`; pax
    support (none observed; can be added under the same bound if the 23138310 containers need it).
  - **Effect:** `EXPAND_MODULES` (expand bundle, regen-batch.md). No existing corpus has a nested `tar.gz`; a gzip that
    is not a tar keeps its current code. The 23138310 containers' header structure is unverified (not staged; a scan
    needs the user's yes for the download).
- **D-58 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: streaming `expand`; HL.R7, D-47 item 3).** `JobContext.open_input(index)` opens a
  store object with the no-follow opener, hashes it in 1 MiB chunks, checks the digest, rewinds and returns the handle
  (`read_input` is built on it). `job_expand` passes that handle to `open_archive`; the nested-`tar.gz` path reads it in
  chunks too (`iter_gzip_bounded` takes a handle). Members are still read whole before their header is sent (a defect
  never yields partial bytes), bounded by `max_member_bytes`. Evidence: `docs/reports/hardening/expand-calibration.md`
  (peak 505 → 134 MiB on a 380 MB archive, CPU unchanged).
  - **Residual:** the bytes are hashed, then read again through the same descriptor. A store object is 0444 and the
    worker cannot write files (`RLIMIT_FSIZE = 0`), so only a writer outside the worker could change it in between.
  - **Rejected:** streaming member bytes into `DATA` frames before the CRC check (a defect would leave a half-sent
    member); `mmap` (the same check-then-use gap, and a platform difference).
  - **Effect:** `raw/members.py` and `ingest/` are `EXPAND_MODULES` (expand bundle); member digests and rows are
    unchanged (the level-2 and SEC-07 tests compare them across worker counts).
- **D-59 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: F-08 applied: a selection-pattern segment holds at most two `*`).** `Selection` refuses
  a pattern with a segment (other than a whole `**`) containing more than two `*` (`raw.members.invalid`), which
  `glob.translate` would compile into a super-linear regex (80 s on a 200-character label). Every shipped pattern has
  at most two (`samples/*_epoch_*.json`), so no selection changes. Part of the expand bundle (D-52's condition).
  - **Rejected:** a custom matcher without backtracking (a selection-semantics risk for no shipped benefit).
- **D-60 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: the expand-job budgets are calibrated and kept; G.11.3 Q13, D-47 item 1).** Measured on
  a seeded synthetic zip (512 MiB selected) and the cached survey `artifact.zip` (652 MiB, 44,281 members): 4–7 s CPU and
  at most 15 s wall per GiB under load, against the provisional +60 s / +120 s per GiB (applied for the full
  `max_total_bytes` to every expand job): at least 10× headroom at the 4 GiB cap. Values unchanged; G.4.3 "As built".
  - **Rejected:** lowering the increments to the measured cost (a slower host or a heavily loaded one would fail jobs
    that are not attacks); scaling by the archive's declared total (the parent does not know it before the worker opens
    the archive).
- **D-61 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: tombstoned digests are blocked at ingest; D-46's open item; finding F-12C-05).**
  `raw/store.py`: `read_tombstones(root)` and `RawObjectStore.tombstoned()` (re-read when the file changes) read
  `tombstones.jsonl` strictly and fail closed; `put_chunks` (so `put`, `put_stream`, the corpus writer and `expand`)
  publishes nothing for a listed digest and returns `PutResult(tombstoned=True)`. `raw/fetch.py`: a pinned SHA-256 listed in
  `<cache>/tombstones.jsonl` raises `raw.fetch.tombstoned` before the transport is used; an MD5-only download that hashes to
  a listed digest is discarded. G.9.6 "As built".
  - **Why:** phase 12c reproduced a re-import after `purge` writing the purged credential back beside its tombstone
    (`tests/security/test_sec25_purge.py::test_sec25_a_reimport_never_stores_a_tombstoned_object_again`, strict xfail
    until this fix, now a pass).
  - **Not raising:** a resumed import must finish (its executions are `skipped_resume`); a raise would abort it. The
    caller that maps a new candidate must look at `tombstoned` and register it instead (routed, R12b-6).
  - **Rejected:** the check in the importer only (the corpus writer, `expand` and the fetcher's git path all write through
    the store; one guard in the store covers them); reading purge's own decoder (`corpus/` must not be imported by
    `raw/`; the store reads only the `sha256` column, strictly).
  - **Effect:** no output byte changes for any corpus without tombstones; `raw/store.py` is not an `EXPAND_MODULES` file.
- **D-62 (2026-10-12, phase 12b: the interpreter guard's wording is narrowed to the entry points that ingest an archive

  M.1/N.1 item 7 and D §0/§D.13.1 listed `package` among the release-mode entry points that refuse below 3.14.8. In this
  build `package` in seal mode opens no archive or compressed stream (proved by
  `tests/security/test_sec26_package.py::test_sec26_package_below_the_floor_opens_no_archive_while_sealing`), so it has
  nothing to refuse; the deposit builder behind `package --deposit` refuses with exit 3, and `package` still refuses an
  advisory corpus with exit 4 (G.3.8(3)). The spec now says so; no code changes.
  - **Rejected:** adding the guard to seal mode (it would refuse an operation that runs no affected parser; phase-11 code).
  - **Consequence:** a corpus sealed below 3.14.8 records the old interpreter in `producer.python` with
    `interpreter_advisory` `null`, since nothing advisory-relevant ran; the deposit builder still refuses to package it
    below the floor.
- **D-90 (2026-10-11, phase 10c: read-only support for a gzip tar nested inside a zip is requested from phase 12; user

- **D-91 (2026-10-11, phase 10c: `:` is allowed inside a component of an archive member label; requested from phase

  - **Rejected:** asserting the code default at class I (no evidence links it to these runs).

- **D-80 (2026-10-12, regeneration-batch item 3: how D-24 and D-27 c6 are implemented; implementer's choices within
  the user-approved item).** Spec D.5.4 "Citation of D rules".
  - (a) **Verification is the catalogue `code` list, matched against the profile's `verified_code`.** Each profile
    lists the commits whose code produced its records, with an optional facet selector (`variant`; `transcript` for
    transcript/v1). A D rule is cited at D only where one of its `code` commits applies; otherwise its I twin
    `<id>_unverified@<n>` is cited. This replaces `structural_rule_class`, which governed four rules. A rule that cites
    no code is never verified (D-27 c6). The verified sets follow the phase-10 analysis and examination 2 (R07b):
    `c274885` for `v0.k11`; `a75aba76` + `089ed468` for `v1.k14` (the 0.1.30+ family); for Mandate, also its script
    `fa62a977`; for adprov-v1, `579a908`, plus `c274885` for converted transcripts; none for ROPE, AgentDyn and survey.
  - (b) **Fail closed.** A D rule that resolves to a missing twin raises `RuleNotDeclared` at map time. Two rules are
    declared independent of the producing code: `agentdojo.system_prompt_variant_digest` and
    `rope.security_correction`. 31 twins were added: agentdojo 18, agentdyn 3, rope 3, adprov 7. The adprov 7 include
    `adprov.empty_assistant_text_ambiguous`, the tenth code-less D rule a mapper cites, under the same c6 reasoning.
  - (c) **Classes follow the rules.** After mapping, every record is weakened per C.6.5 rule 1: a field whose
    applicable rule is I is I, and a D record cited unscoped by an I rule is I. A causal `after` edge on a twinned
    `generated_by` link is weakened with it. The weakening never raises a class and does not fire on any pre-change
    AER (checked on all 77 real fixtures).
  - (d) **Seal issues** cite their rule as given, except the issues that report a statement's reading (retry,
    last-pass, run-error), which cite the resolved rule.
  - (e) **Completeness (B6):** a loss issue proves loss (H.3.2(2)) only when its rule is class D, so an inferred retry
    leaves the execution `unverifiable`. `incomplete_run` keeps its D rule: the missing outcome or duration keys are
    observed.
  - (f) **Census and the artefact net** count a twin as its D rule's reading. One adprov entry was added:
    `adprov.art.single_attempt_inferred`.
  - **Why:** one mechanism, machine-checkable (the R07b test over every real fixture), and usable unchanged by the
    phase-10d profiles (`verified_code = []`).
  - **Rejected:** a per-profile list of rules to twin (not checkable against the evidence); keeping
    `structural_rule_class` and adding ternaries per rule (the C6 gap would reopen with every new rule); verifying the
    June-2024-only rules at `089ed468` now to keep head `v1.k14` at D (a research act per rule, not item 3; possible
    later as a code citation and a new rule version); twins for issue-only rules (an issue is not a statement).
  - **Addendum (d) (2026-10-15; regeneration-batch item 103; user decision in the regen-items window, from the corpus
    pre-check's refuted PC-ast-survey-agentdojo-01).** `unexecuted_tool_call` and `missing_tool_result` join the
    issues that report a statement's reading. Since item 24 the issue is a PROV premise: "this call was not
    dispatched", and for `missing_tool_result` a loss (H.3.2(2)). Both conclusions read the harness's behaviour. So the
    TraceLogger and DRIFT builds cite the resolved rule (`self.cite.cite`), which under `verified_code = []` is the new
    class-I twin `agentdojo.unexecuted_trailing_calls_unverified@1`.
    - **Effect:** the not-dispatched statement goes to the inference bundle. A missing result proves no loss. The
      accounting checks still mark the execution `inconsistent` where calls were not handled once. Verified code
      (agentdojo-upstream's c274885, for example) keeps the D rule.
    - The earlier rejection of "twins for issue-only rules" is narrowed: an issue that item 24 makes a premise reports
      a reading.
    - **Rejected:** keeping them as given (a D citation of unverified harness behaviour, against D-24).
- **D-81 (2026-10-12, engine: an attribute that names an INFERRED node is routed out of a stronger element; a core
  correctness fix recorded per invariant 5).** Item 3 makes attempt scopes and model calls INFERRED for unverified
  harnesses. Core activities then named them in `apv:partOf` / `apv:afterCausal`, which tier 4 refuses
  (`pv.prov_structure.core_undeclared`). `agentprov-prov/0.1` now gives such an attribute the INFERRED class after all
  statements are classified, so the existing split (E.1.5 item 5) moves it to the inference bundle (C.6.5 rule 4).
  The cap applies only to INFERRED targets. Deriving all 77 real-fixture AERs from before item 3 with and without the
  cap gives byte-identical PROV, and all 1,056 AgentHarm executions re-derive to their stored SEM and PROV bytes.
  - **Why:** rule 4 already says a statement is at most the class of what it names; the gap was latent because no
    attempt scope was INFERRED before item 3.
  - **Rejected:** citing a twin at `/scope` on every record of an inferred attempt (bloats every AER);
    keeping attempt scopes at D (their reading rests on the unverified harness); the full rule-4 cap for O and D
    targets (it would change the `apv:derivedAttribute` lists of existing corpora, outside item 3; noted for the
    batch).
- **D-82 (2026-10-12, the DTap partial trajectory is `unverifiable`; decision delegated by the user).** DTap's one
  `partial_trajectory.json` raises `incomplete_run` under `dtap.partial_file_name@1`, class I: the file name is the
  only evidence of truncation. Under H.3.2(2) as clarified by item 3 (D-80 (e)), a loss issue proves loss only under a
  class-D rule, so the run's completeness is `unverifiable`, not the `known_incomplete` §D.16 stated. D-29 item 8 is
  unchanged: the run is imported with `dtap.partial_trajectory` and `incomplete_run`, and no gap is filled. It stays
  in rates as before. No DTap corpus existed, so no bytes change.
  - **Why:** the same reason as B6 (D-24): an inferred loss is disclosed, not proven. A file name is a claim about

  - **Rejected:** a DTap exception in the completeness rule (an I rule would again prove loss); raising
    `dtap.partial_file_name` to D (it rests on no code and on no observed content).
- **D-83 (2026-10-12, an annotation INFERRED by propagation takes its PROV method from its premises; fix of an item-3
  regression found by the full suite after the merge).** Under item 3 a judgement's `/origin` can rest on an
  `_unverified` twin (e.g. `agentdojo.checker_outcome` on `v1.k14` logs), so SEM outcome annotations over it are

  - **Why:** C.6.5 rules 3 and 4 already say the class and method come from the weakest premise. Twins for the SEM
    rules are a separate question (open question 3), and the twin in the premise already names the method.
  - **Rejected:** adding SEM-rule twins now (it belongs to item 1's `agentdojo.suites@2`, and it would still need this
    path for annotations INFERRED only through their premises); raising the SEM rule's class to I (it would drop the
    annotations of verified harnesses to I).
  - **Tests:** `tests/adapters/test_code_verification.py` maps, annotates, derives and runs tier 4 on a `v1.k14` log
    with twins and on one real fixture per affected profile. The prediction now re-maps a sample of each stored corpus
    and runs SEM, PROV and tier 4 (release) on it (`regen-batch.md`).
- **D-84 (2026-10-12, head `v0.k11` logs introduced after `c274885` cite the twins; user decision on open question 1 of
  item 3, relayed by the orchestrating session and confirmed by the user).** A `v0.k11` log's producing code is
  verified by the June-2024 citations only if the commit that introduced its blob (the git origin's
  `introduced_in_commit`, from the history index) is `c274885` or one of its ancestors. A log introduced later (0.1.29-era

  introducing commit (imported without the history index) is treated the same way (fail closed). Regeneration-batch

- **D-89 (2026-10-12, tier-4 round trip: one encoding and one parse per serialisation, released early; step 1 of the
  phase-11 hot-spot proposals).** `validate/roundtrip.py` now encodes the document and writes its TriG once (under the
  surrogate names). It parses that text once and uses the parsed dataset for three purposes: the model decode, which
  is what `ProvDocument.deserialize` does with the same text; the graph comparison; and the completeness check, which
  reads the image with each surrogate namespace mapped back to its real IRI. Before, completeness re-encoded and
  re-parsed the real-named document, and the first TriG text was parsed twice. The first model is released before
  the second is encoded, and the graphs are compared one named graph at a time. The TriG text round trip itself is
  unchanged.
  - **Evidence:** 30 executions (the largest and median AERs of every corpus, re-mapped from raw; two DTap runs of
    5.8 and 14.7 MB of PROV) give byte-identical tier-4 reports before and after. The validation unit and PROV suites
    pass. Interleaved timing of the round trip on a shared machine: ROPE 2.5 MB PROV 21–26 s → 11–17 s (304 → 278 MB),
    DTap 5.8 MB 37–67 s → 24–36 s (peak ~590 MB, unchanged), head 0.8 MB about the same.
  - **Not solved by step 1:** the DTap peak (1.5–1.7 GB for 14.7 MB of PROV). Proposals 2 (N-Quads instead of TriG)
    and 3 (comparing canonical N-Quads lines instead of a second decode) change which serialisation the check
    exercises, so they were evaluated separately (step 2 below).
  - **Rejected:** comparing the in-memory encoding instead of the parsed text (it would stop testing the TriG writer
    and parser).
  - **Step 2 (addendum, 2026-10-12; proposals 2 and 3 adopted).** The round trip writes N-Quads instead of TriG and
    parses only the first text: the decode and the completeness check read that parse, and the second encoding is
    compared with the first as sets of N-Quads lines per graph, not parsed. On the largest DTap run the TriG writer
    took 8.3 s per text and the N-Quads writer 0.9 s; rdflib parses N-Quads more slowly (7.7 s against 5.5 s), so
    only one text is parsed. The texts are kept as bytes. The parsed image gets the encoding's namespace bindings,
    which a TriG text declared: the decoder names IRIs by them, so a failed model comparison names records with the
    document's prefixes, not minted `ns1:` ones. A blank node counts as lost and added, as it did when both texts were
    parsed. Completeness runs after the first model is released and before the second encoding.
    - **Evidence:** the 30 executions give byte-identical tier-4 reports to those before D-89 (tier 4 381 s → 132 s in total for the 30, under load; step 1 gave 305 s). 81 crafted documents (control
      characters, quotes, `>`, lone surrogates, odd local names and bundle names) give the outcomes of step 1 except
      three, all with a raw line break in a name: TriG writes such an IRI unescaped and its parser accepts it; N-Quads
      rejects it, so step 2 reports `pv.roundtrip.load`. The tier-4 structure check already rejects every such name
      (`pv.prov_structure.qname`), so no document that passes it changes. Process CPU time, step 1 → step 2,
      interleaved under load: ROPE 2.5 MB PROV 6.7–8.2 → 5.0–5.3 s, head 0.8 MB 2.2 → 1.5 s, adprov 13 → 9.3 s,
      DTap 14.7 MB 44–55 → 41–45 s. DTap peak RSS of the round trip 1,509–1,579 → 1,302–1,419 MB.
    - **What it no longer tests:** the TriG writer and parser. TriG stays the on-demand output (`derive --trig`,
      E.5.4) and is not part of the sealed corpus; the round trip now tests the N-Quads writer and parser.
    - **Still not solved:** most of the DTap peak is the first model held together with its rdflib encoding
      (~0.85 GB); the `prov` API encodes from a whole model. The worker RSS cap (`worker.py`) is phase 12's and is
      unchanged.
    - **Rejected:** parsing the second text too (7.7 s on DTap for no change in any finding); hashing the lines
      (smaller, but equality would no longer be exact).

    0.3.130, 0.3.134.dev31, 0.3.154.dev37 and 0.3.159.dev20).** The losses are explained by code, and the Inspect mapper
    now recovers the links under three class-D rules: `inspect.message_copies_share_calls@1` (copies of one message made
    by `model_copy` in `_remove_submit_tool` and `resolve_reasoning_history` share their calls; the call is the produced
    copy's), `inspect.tool_event_message_id_first_of_batch@1` (`execute_tools` gives every event of a parallel batch the
    first call's result message id; where `message_id` names another call's result, the result is found by call id), and
    `inspect.react_submit_message_removed@1` (react removes the submit result message; the event's `result` becomes an
    artefact the execution generated, and the absence is declared as `missing_tool_result` citing that rule). Copies'
    call parts are declared `unexecuted_tool_call` under the copy rule. Measured on the scratch WhistleBench import:

  - **Addendum 2 (2026-10-13, regeneration-batch item 25; user-approved, with the fetch of 0.3.112..0.3.129).**
    `ToolEvent.message_id` first appears at 0.3.113, and that release already writes it as `result_messages[0].id`. So
    the first-of-batch defect starts at 0.3.113, and its rule gains that code citation.

    - **Follow-ups (user-approved, deferrals session):** carved blobs replace the digests with `$blob` references;
