- **D-160 (2026-10-12, fix F-12C-01: a reference under raw policy `include` is a `chain` failure; user-approved 2026-10-12).** `chain` accepts a not-stored raw object behind a `raw/REFERENCES.json` entry only when a snapshot it
  belongs to declares raw policy `reference` in `corpus.json` (H.4.1). The object's snapshots are those of the index rows
  that list it, its outermost container or its members (`raw/members.jsonl`); an object no row lists belongs to every
  snapshot. Otherwise the finding is `raw.reference.not_permitted`, status **failed** (exit 1 in dev and release mode).
  The legitimate case (a `reference`-policy snapshot; H.4.2's DRIFT history blobs, the `ciaware-bench` parts) is told
  apart by what the manifest declares, not by the entry's `reason`. A working manifest declares no raw policy (it is
  set at sealing), so a working tree keeps the earlier behaviour. This build seals only single-policy corpora and writes
  no `REFERENCES.json`, so no legitimate corpus changes outcome.
  - **Rejected:** status `unverified` (it would pass dev mode, and the manifest contradicts the file: a declared
    `include` snapshot with a referenced object is an inconsistency, not a skipped check); refusing every
    `REFERENCES.json` in a sealed corpus (breaks `reference`-policy snapshots, H.4.1); deciding by the entry's `reason`
    field (corpus-supplied, untrusted, R-43).
- **D-161 (2026-10-12, fix F-12C-04: the Markdown format of `stats` escapes every cell; user-approved
  2026-10-12).** `stats` labels pass `escape_untrusted_line` (one line), and every Markdown cell and the corpus heading
  pass `escape_markdown` (G.8.2 "One-line labels"), closed-vocabulary columns included. The `text`, `csv` and `json`
  formats are byte-identical to before on the four existing working corpora compared (with the `fn_digest`, the hash
  of the stats sources, normalised). The one benign Markdown change is the `pointer` column of the `unknowns` table:
  `/parts/<k>...` is now written `/parts/&lt;k>...` (12 rows over the four corpora). A Markdown renderer read the old
  `<k>` as an HTML tag and dropped it, so the new bytes render as the pointer is written and the old ones did not.
  - **Rejected:** escaping only the data-derived columns (`model`, `artefact_id`, failure details) to keep those 12 rows
    byte-identical (a per-column list that a new table or column can silently miss, and it keeps the mis-rendering);
    leaving `<` alone when the text is closed vocabulary (the renderer cannot tell).
- **D-162 (2026-10-12, proposal P-1 implemented: orphan execution files fail `chain` on a sealed corpus; user-approved
  2026-10-12).** On a sealed corpus (tree or archive), every file present whose H.1.3 role is `aer`, `sem` or
  `prov` must be a path an index row names (`aer`, `sem[profile]`, `prov[spec]`); otherwise `index.orphan` (failed).
  This narrows the D-39/D-63 boundary: an orphan added with regenerated checksums is no longer detected by the root
  digest alone. Working trees are not checked (they need not be closed-world until sealed), but sealing runs `chain` in
  release mode, so a working tree that holds orphans is now refused at sealing. Of the existing working corpora under
  `~/.agentprov/corpora`, only `agentdyn-a-p10.pre-integration.partial` holds orphans (388); the current `*-p10.partial`
  trees hold none.
  - **Rejected:** reporting orphans `unverified` (they are bytes in a sealed deposit that no digest chain covers, the
    exact gap P-1 names); checking working trees too (an interrupted import or a dropped SEM profile can leave stale
    files there legitimately until sealing).
- **D-163 (2026-10-12, proposal P-2 implemented: `schemas/**`, `WITHHELD.json` and `views/` are reconciled by `chain`;
  user-approved 2026-10-12).** On a sealed corpus: every `schemas/<name>` present, and the two schemas
  sealing writes (`aer-0.1.schema.json`, `corpus-0.1.schema.json`), must equal the installed package's resource of that
  name byte for byte (`schemas.mismatch`, failed; a name outside the three published schemas is a mismatch; a schema the
  package does not ship is `schemas.unavailable`, unverified). `WITHHELD.json` present but not declared in the
  manifest's `files` is `withheld.undeclared` (a declared one is checked by `manifest.files`). A `views/` file needs a
  `views` stage in `derivation.json` and an index row for its execution (`views.undeclared`). Consequence: a published
  schema is frozen with its version, like the format it describes; changing the bytes of `aer-0.1.schema.json` or
  `corpus-0.1.schema.json` in a later package would make every corpus sealed earlier fail `chain`, so a schema change
  bumps the schema's version (new file name).
  - **Rejected:** recording schema digests in the manifest and comparing against those (it needs a manifest format
    change, and a forger regenerates the manifest anyway; the package is the authority, as for `rules/**`, AD-14);
    reconciling `raw/REFERENCES.json` with `files.references` in the same change (outside P-2; noted for the
    orchestrator).
- **D-200 (2026-10-12, deferrals part A: archive inputs; user-approved with the merge of part A).** A download pin's
  file (a Zenodo or Hugging Face file) whose members are whole run logs is an **archive input**: `import --input FILE
  --verify-against-pin` (or `--fetch` from the verified cache) stores the file with the pin's origin (`zenodo {doi,
  file}`, `hf {repo, revision, path}`), expands it in place through the versioned `expand` stage with the profile's
  `include`, `blobs` and context-artefact globs as the selection (AD-12; never extracted; members outside the selection
  are `not_selected` rows and are never decompressed), and maps every selected member as a whole file with its `member`
  origin. Register subjects of members are `<file>!/<member>`; the working manifest's snapshot records `input {kind:
  archive, label, sha256, bytes}`; `recompute` re-expands the stored container (`StoredRawTree.archive_input`); sealing
  builds the snapshot origin `{kind: zenodo, doi, file, md5?}` (H.2.3). An archive of a container dialect (an archive
  inside an archive) is refused (exit 5); a `.zip` under a git pin stays refused. The mapper side (the TraceLogger mapper
  reading the layout from a `member` origin's `label`, D-156 part 2) is the mapper owner's (D-204).
  - **Why:** every Zenodo source needs it (phase 10f's D-154/D-156, phase 10g's 23168099, phase 10i's AgentOps-Bench);
    the existing `expand` stage and its limits (SEC-05) already gate archive members, so no new parsing surface is added.
  - **Rejected:** a separate "archive tree" walk parsing the central directory in T0 (archive parsing belongs in T1,
    G.4); registering every `not_selected` member (its `raw/members.jsonl` row is its disposition, R-40); member
    subjects without the container prefix (a re-map could not tell them from the container's own rows).
- **D-201 (2026-10-12, deferrals part A: the Zenodo pin record; user-approved with the merge of part A).** A Zenodo pin records the version DOI, the
  record id (`record`, optional, must equal the DOI's), the version label (`version`, optional), the file name, its
  size (`bytes`/`size`) and its digests (`sha256`, required for an import; `md5` as the deposit's transport check).
  `--verify-against-pin` checks a local file offline: file name, size, MD5 when pinned, SHA-256
  (`raw.fetch.verify_download`; `raw.fetch.digest` on a mismatch, `raw.fetch.unverifiable` without a SHA-256). The
  working manifest's snapshot `pin` holds the whole record (git and listing pins keep their phase-6 projection).
  `--fetch` of a download pin of 100 MiB or more needs `--i-consent-to-large-download` (U-07), as `agentprov fetch`.
  - **Why:** the deposit is the origin; its record id and version identify it on Zenodo, its digest identifies the bytes.
  - **Rejected:** fetching the record's metadata to check the version label (network for every import; the label is a
    deposit claim, recorded as such); MD5 alone (the raw store and every AER artefact are SHA-256 addressed).
- **D-202 (2026-10-12, deferrals part A: several snapshots per corpus; resolves the spec drift of D-64; user-approved with the merge of part A).** One
  corpus may hold several snapshots of its one source through one source profile (H.1.1(1)): a later `import` into the
  same working corpus with another `--snapshot` adds it (G4 still refuses another corpus id, source, mode or profile).
  H.7.2 is implemented: a primary artefact another snapshot already mapped is not mapped again; its row lists the new
  snapshot in `snapshot_ids`, its new origin is a `raw/origins.jsonl` row (`n_origins` recounted), and a
  `dedup.collapsed` entry records it. The AER of a shared execution carries the origin of the snapshot that imported it
  first; the manifest keeps the snapshots in import order (each with its `part` once there are several) and `recompute`
  and `verify --level rederive` replay them in that order, each from the objects its pin vouched for
  (`origin_matches_pin`), so a re-map is byte-identical. Sealing takes each snapshot's origin from the origins its pin
  vouched for. **D-35 stands:** `agentdojo-upstream` is released as two corpora; a one-corpus, two-snapshot AgentDojo
  tree is a supported layout used for scratch comparisons. Spec: H.4.2's `agentdojo-upstream` row, H.7.2, N.2.2's
  `--snapshot` row and N.2.2(7) are reconciled to this.
  - **Why:** the user asked for the refusal to be lifted; H.7.2 is the spec's own rule, and D-35 is a release decision,
    not a format limit.
  - **Rejected:** re-sealing earlier AERs to a canonical snapshot order (rewrites sealed records); origin-free AERs (an
    `aer/0.1` change); corpus-scoped execution ids (rejected in D-35 too).
- **D-203 (2026-10-12, deferrals part A: import-side blob storage; user-approved with the merge of part A).** A profile's `[import] blobs` globs name
  files that hold blob payloads AER records reference by digest (`$blob`, C.11.5; FooBench's screenshot). They are
  stored before mapping with their pinned origins (store-first; one the pin does not vouch for is
  `raw.origin.blob_mismatch`), never mapped and never registered, and every map job is offered, as `blob:<hex>`, the blob
  files in its primary's directory or below (the capture family's contract, D.10.4a), so a mapper can check a declared
  size; AER-V21 finds them in the raw store and the seal lists the referenced ones (`seal.blobs`). Blobs are raw evidence
  (C.11.5): a blob a mapper derives from an artefact (Inspect's condensed requests, DTap's long strings) needs an origin
  kind `aer/0.1` does not have and is left to the `aer/0.2` design (part C).
  - **Rejected:** offering every blob to every job (job inputs grow with the square of the tree); finding blobs by
    hashing every non-candidate file (reads every file of a tree); listing blobs as unit artefacts (a unit would claim
    blobs it never references).
- **D-204 (2026-10-12, deferrals part A: the member-origin interface for mappers; user-approved with the merge of part A; the mapper side is regen-batch item 18).**
  For an archive input, the `origin` a whole-file map job receives is a `member` origin `{container, label, method,
  crc32, size}`. Its `label` is the member's NFC name, the same string the profile's `include` globs and layout
  templates were matched against, so a mapper that reads a git origin's `path` for its layout (the TraceLogger mapper,
  `adapters/agentdojo/mapper.py`, locator `{"a": "a0", "o": "/path"}`) reads `/label` for a `member` origin (phase 10f
  routing F2). The runner change does not touch any mapper; the mapper change is the regen-batch session's and moves no
  stored AER (no stored corpus has a member-origin AgentDojo log).
- **D-205 (2026-10-12, deferrals part B: the full-history store and index; user-approved with the merge of part B).** AgentDojo's full history (bare,
  the head pin's history with all blobs, no checkout; user-approved fetch, 37.8 MB packed) lives at
  `$AGENTPROV_HOME/upstream/github.com/ethz-spylab/agentdojo.git`, beside the blobless store the history table uses,
  never in the repository and never in a corpus. `agentprov.raw.history` gains the full-history index
  (`FullHistoryIndex`, format `agentprov-history-index-full/1`): every `(path, blob)` ever added under `runs/` with its
  introducing commit by the pinned indexes' own rule and the pins that hold it; 48,605 versions, 7,867 superseded. It is
  derived data, rebuilt by `tools/agentdojo/full_history_index.py`, which also byte-compares the pinned indexes.
  - **Rejected:** a second, differently defined history index (the brief: extend, not duplicate); storing the full
    store in the fetch cache (its blobs must never mix with the depth-1 store's promisor-free objects).
- **D-206 (2026-10-12, deferrals part B: D-84's missing introducing commits are decided by evidence; user-approved with
  the merge of part B).** The two
  cached pinned indexes are byte-identical to the indexes recomputed from the full store, and the full index agrees with
  them row for row, so every pinned blob has an introducing commit. D-84's "no introducing commit" occurs only for an
  import made without the index; its fail-closed treatment (the `_unverified` twins) stays. No byte changes.
- **D-207 (2026-10-12, deferrals part B: the `v0.k11` system prompt; user-approved 2026-10-12, relayed by the
  orchestrator; implemented by the regen-batch session as its item 17).** The
  default system message of AgentDojo had one code state over its whole history (`system_messages.yaml` `default`,
  digest `a021a92b…`, at all 547 commits that carry the file), and 27,866 of the 28,973 pinned `v0.k11` logs carry
  exactly that text, equal to the state at their introducing commit; the other 900 are the `spotlighting_with_delimiting`
  defence, which rewrites the prompt. Proposed: extend `agentdojo-upstream`'s `agentdojo_default` variant to `v0.k11`
  (regen-batch item 17, written up by the regen-batch session), reversing the phase-6/10 choice that kept these logs unlabelled for want of a covering pin: the
  label states a fact about the text, which the history now shows. The code-range measurements for part C (only
  `duration_scope`, `incomplete_run` and partly `call_id_unique_match` keep their cited passages over
  `c274885..<introducing commit>`) are in `docs/reports/deferrals/part-b/README.md` §4.
  - **Rejected:** labelling by the producing code (not recorded; the introducing commit bounds it from above only).
  - **Implemented (2026-10-12, regeneration-batch item 17, on main at `b7b86b6`; the user's yes also given in the
    regen-batch session).** The spotlighting logs are labelled, not flagged or left out (the owner's choice): their two
    texts are the default plus the defence's sentence in its two code states, `agentdojo_default_spotlighting_2024_06`
    (`d9524c73…`, typographic apostrophe, `c274885`) and `agentdojo_default_spotlighting` (`2954962b…`, after
    `40085c0`), both restricted to `v0.k11` and the `*-spotlighting_with_delimiting` run directory. Every `v0.k11` log
    with a system message is labelled (2024-06 18,034 of 18,241; head 24,707 of 24,914); the full-derive sample check
    found PROV statements unchanged apart from digests. The `history` part's note now counts 7,867 versions held by
    neither pin (11,173 is the distinct blobs absent from head, 4,059 of them in the 2024-06 part).
- **D-230 (2026-10-12, withholding session: the `agentprov-withheld/0.1` format; user-approved 2026-10-13).** `WITHHELD.json` is a corpus-layer single JSON document `{format, entries, executions, policies}` with a
  new published schema `schemas/withheld-0.1.schema.json`. It is generated from `agentprov.corpus.withheld` and frozen
  with its version (D-163). A sealed corpus that holds `WITHHELD.json` also holds a copy of that schema, and `chain`
  compares the copy byte for byte with the package's. `entries` keeps G.9.5's object shape and adds `basis` (`purge`,
  `raw_policy`, `profile_rule`, `container`). `bytes`, `media_type`, `finding` and `decided_on` are nullable and never
  filled with placeholders. `origins` holds the object's `raw/origins.jsonl` origins (at least one). `executions` gives
  each withheld execution's id, snapshots and stage digests (the index row's `digests`), so it can be recomputed
  locally from the pin and checked. `policies` names the profile `[withhold]` policy applied: rule ids, kinds and
  scopes, never a marker or pattern. Neither the value nor any fragment of it is recorded. The source key is not kept
  either, because its locator can hold source-derived names (D-146's account paths).
  - **Why:** G.9.5 fixes the object shape. Recomputing an execution needs its identity and digests, and the document
    must stay safe to publish.
  - **Rejected:** keeping only G.9.5's `entries` (a withheld execution could not be checked after a local recompute);
    recording the source key (it can carry personal paths); copying the profile's markers or patterns (they live in
    `rules/<profile>.profile.toml`).
- **D-231 (2026-10-12, withholding: the sealed tree is what is released; a private sidecar keeps the rest; user-approved 2026-10-13).**
  A withheld execution leaves the sealed corpus. Its index row leaves `executions.jsonl`, its validation row leaves
  `validation/` (`summary.json` is recomputed from the remaining rows by the writer's own function), and its AER, SEM,
  PROV and view files leave the tree. A withheld object's bytes leave `raw/objects/`. Its `raw/origins.jsonl` and
  `raw/members.jsonl` rows stay, and so does `raw/tombstones.jsonl`. Sealing **renames** these files into `DIR.withheld/`
  beside the sealed `DIR` (mode 0700): the same relative paths, plus the withheld index rows, their validation rows and
  a copy of `WITHHELD.json`. It never deletes them, rolls the renames back if sealing fails, and refuses an existing
  sidecar. The sidecar is not a corpus, has no checksums, and is never deposited; deleting it is the user's decision.
  The register keeps every entry of a withheld execution. Its `release.withheld` entry (stage `package`, disposition
  `withheld`) is added when missing.
  - **Consequence for the counts (H.6.1 R1/R5):** the frozen corpus-0.1 manifest has no `withheld` count, so a sealed
    corpus counts its released executions. `candidates == executions + not_imported` holds over them. The withheld
    executions are counted in `WITHHELD.json` and in `counts.issues_by_code["release.withheld"]`, and the datasheet
    states the number. `records_by_kind`, `models` and `framework_identities` cover the released AERs only.
  - **Why:** a deposit is the sealed tree, and archive-mode `verify` checks it closed-world. If a sealed corpus kept
    withheld files that the deposit lacked, the `checksums` level could not verify a deposit. Keeping the rows with
    their files gone would break every consumer that reads AERs (`stats`, `render`, `recompute`), and their facets could
    carry a fragment.
  - **Rejected:** a complete private sealed corpus with deposit-side filtering (a deposit that fails its own
    checksums); index rows kept in working form (consumers break, facets may leak); deleting the withheld files (the
    task rules forbid deleting data); a `withheld` count in the manifest (a corpus-0.2 schema for one integer).
- **D-232 (2026-10-12, withholding: purge to release, P-3; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Every object listed in `raw/tombstones.jsonl`
  is withheld: basis `purge`, with the reason and date from the tombstone. So are the executions that cite it or, for a
  container, one of its members (the set `purge` gave `release.withheld`). An archive that holds a withheld member is
  withheld at object level (basis `container`). Its other members, stored as their own objects, stay. Release-mode
  `chain` accepts a tombstone exactly when `WITHHELD.json` lists the object (counter `tombstoned_withheld`). Otherwise
  it still reports `raw.tombstoned` (tombstoned, failing release mode). A `release.withheld` register entry that no
  tombstone, `withhold` snapshot or profile rule explains refuses the seal (`corpus.withhold.unexplained`, exit 4).
  - **Why:** G.9.5 and H.1.2 already say a purged object is withheld from a new version. The acceptance is tied to
    `WITHHELD.json`, so a forged tombstone over an object that the ledger does not list still fails.
  - **Rejected:** accepting every tombstone in a sealed corpus (it hides a deleted object, the SEC-15 forgery row);
    inferring withholding from the register alone (an unexplained entry would withhold with no recorded cause).
- **D-233 (2026-10-12, withholding: raw policy `withhold` per snapshot; user-approved 2026-10-13).** A snapshot with raw policy
  `withhold` releases nothing. Every execution that a row of that snapshot records is withheld, including a row shared
  with another snapshot (*withhold wins*). So is every object such a row cites, and every object whose origin the
  snapshot's pin vouched for (members follow their container). The reason is `licence`. The released snapshots must
  share one raw policy, which `licences.policy.raw_policy` records. When every snapshot is `withhold`, the corpus raw
  policy is `withhold`, and a sealed but unreleasable record can be built for any licence policy except `forbidden`
  (withholding only narrows a release). The deposit builder refuses a corpus whose raw policy is `withhold`, and
  accepts a `withhold` snapshot only alongside a `WITHHELD.json`. `chain` fails an index row of a `withhold` snapshot
  (`withheld.policy`).
  - **Why:** H.4.1 sets the policy per snapshot, and part A brought several snapshots per corpus.
  - **Rejected:** *include wins* for a shared object (it would release bytes on the strength of the other origin's
    licence reading; a user who wants that can split the corpus, D-35); refusing every corpus with a `withhold` snapshot
    (the old H.4.1 table row, written for one-snapshot corpora).
- **D-234 (2026-10-12, withholding: the source-profile `[withhold]` policy; user-approved 2026-10-13; includes a one-line edit of
  `adapters/profiles.py`, cleared by the orchestrator).** A source profile may declare `[withhold]`:
  - table keys: `reason`, `public_note` (one line, at most 200 characters), and optionally `scan_rules` (release-scan
    rule ids);
  - `[[withhold.rules]]` entries: each has an `id` and either a literal `marker` (4 to 256 characters, a tag such as
    `(token:`, never a secret value) or a bounded `pattern`, plus an optional `scope` (`executions`, the default, or
    `object`) and optional per-rule `reason` and `public_note`.

  At sealing, every stored raw object and every derived file (AER, SEM, PROV, view) of every execution is scanned in
  1 MiB chunks with overlap. A raw hit withholds the object, and with scope `executions` also the executions that cite
  it. A derived hit always withholds that execution and its primary object, because the value came from the raw
  evidence, perhaps in another encoding. Only rule ids are kept, never a match.
  - **Pattern grammar:** atoms (an ASCII literal, escaped punctuation, `\d`, `\w`, `\s`, a character class), each
    with `?`, `{n}` or `{m,n}` (n ≤ 256). There are no groups, alternation, `.`, `*`, `+` or anchors, so every match has
    a known maximum length and matching cannot backtrack badly on untrusted bytes.
  - **Reading the policy:** sealing, `chain` and the deposit builder all read it through `policy_of_profile`, from the
    in-package profile or from its digest-checked copy under `rules/`.
  - **Loader:** `adapters/profiles.py` admits `withhold` in `_TOP_LEVEL`, a one-line cross-folder edit the
    orchestrator cleared. That file is in no `code_sha256`, so no digest moves. It does not validate the table, because
    adapters/ sits below corpus/; `corpus/withhold.py` validates it. No shipped profile declares one yet, so the
    end-to-end tests inject a policy at `policy_of_profile`: the T1 import worker reloads the profile by id from the
    package. The first shipped profile that declares `[withhold]` (expected: Zenodo 22737462, phase-10e rank 5) must
    replace that injection with a real end-to-end test.
  - **Why:** D-146 asks for a canary policy in the profile (as DTap option B). A literal or bounded scan is offline,
    deterministic and testable without gitleaks.
  - **Rejected:** a policy in the corpus spec (it is source knowledge, the same for every corpus of that source);
    unrestricted regular expressions (catastrophic backtracking on hostile bytes; chunk overlap unknown); running
    gitleaks at sealing (`corpus/` runs no subprocess; G.9.4's scan is the backstop).
- **D-235 (2026-10-12, withholding: object-level and execution-level withholding; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Object scope withholds a
  raw object while the executions that cite it stay released, for the case where their derived records never held
  the value (DTap's `env_vars`, which the mapper never reads). Such an execution's AER still names the object in
  `artifacts[]`; `chain` counts it as withheld (`raw_withheld`) instead of missing. If a derived file of such an
  execution hits a rule anyway, the execution is withheld too, so the scope claim is checked, not trusted.
  - **Rejected:** always withholding the citing executions (it would drop executions that hold no value, e.g. DTap's
    4,139); never escalating an object-scope hit (it would trust the profile's claim).
- **D-236 (2026-10-12, withholding: the backstops; user-approved 2026-10-13).** `chain` re-applies the source profile's `[withhold]`
  policy, read from the `rules/` copy, to every released file except `rules/**`, `schemas/**` and `checksums.sha256`.
  A match is `withheld.rule_hit` (failed). Sealing runs `chain` in release mode, so a seal whose withholding missed
  something fails. The deposit builder repeats the rescan (`release.refused.withhold_rule`). It also refuses a
  release-scan finding whose rule the policy's `scan_rules` names unless it is triaged `false-positive`
  (`release.refused.withhold_scan`), so a missed canary never passes as `synthetic-benchmark`. G.9.4's gitleaks scan
  stays the independent backstop.
  - **Further `chain` checks:** `withheld.invalid`, `withheld.present` (withheld bytes or files in the tree),
    `withheld.row`, `withheld.unregistered`, `withheld.unlisted`, `withheld.origins`, `withheld.policy`,
    `withheld.policy_invalid`, plus the schema copy.
  - **Rejected:** trusting `WITHHELD.json.policies` (an absent ledger cannot show that a policy was applied with no
    hits); scanning `rules/` (the profile copy holds the markers themselves).
- **D-237 (2026-10-12, withholding: `raw/REFERENCES.json` reconciled with `files.references`; the open item of
  fix-12c-findings; user-approved 2026-10-13).** Sealing declares `raw/REFERENCES.json` in `files.references` when it is present.
  `chain` reports an undeclared one as `references.undeclared` (failed, sealed corpora), and `manifest.files` checks a
  declared one. `digests.raw_set` now carries the H.2.11 dispositions `referenced` and `withheld` beside `included`, all
  computed by one function (`manifest.raw_dispositions`) shared by sealing, `chain` and the test forger.
  - **No existing corpus changes:** nothing in this build writes `REFERENCES.json` or `WITHHELD.json`. A corpus that
    withholds nothing and references nothing keeps the same raw set, manifest and datasheet bytes.
  - **Rejected:** leaving `raw_set` as "included" only (it contradicts H.2.11 and lets a withheld object vanish from the
    digest chain).
- **D-170 (2026-10-12, phase 10g: one OpenHands event-stream family; approved by the user, 2026-10-12).** A new family
  `openhands` with dialect `openhands.events` and two variants chosen from the event vocabulary: `oas-0.28` (no `system`
  event; browser and NPC `chat` actions; OpenAgentSafety's fork `adityasoni9998/OpenHands@sotopia_chat_tool`, locked as
  `openhands-ai 0.28.1`) and `oh-1.5` (first event `system` with `openhands_version`; RedCode-Exec of Zenodo 23168099).
  One profile per source (`openagentsafety`, `redcode-exec-openhands`), one corpus each (D-144). Logical run identity:
  OAS `(model dir, task)`, RedCode `(model, target, language, "<scenario>_<payload>")`; the case hash in RedCode file
  names is shared across models and kept in `ext` only. Evidence: `docs/reports/phase10g/` (census of all 7,020 runs).
  - **Rejected:** one family per source (the two variants share the event model and the `cause` link); variant by
    version string alone (OAS logs no version).
- **D-171 (2026-10-12, phase 10g: event mapping; approved by the user, 2026-10-12).** One AER per trajectory, events in array order: each
  distinct `model_response` is a `model_call` with an assistant message (reasoning, text and every `tool_call` of the
  response); each tool action is a `tool_execution` whose `call` is the part with its `tool_call_id` and whose `args` are
  OpenHands' dispatched args; each observation is a `tool` message whose `tool_result` answers that call; `system`
  gives the `system_prompt` and `tool_definitions` fixtures and the harness version. Table in
  `docs/reports/phase10g/README.md` §6.1.
  - **Rejected:** one message per action (splits parallel calls of one response, 78 OAS responses); taking tool-call
    arguments only from the action `args` (they are OpenHands' normalised form, not the model's output).
- **D-172 (2026-10-12, phase 10g: `cause` is the link evidence; approved by the user, 2026-10-12).** An observation's `cause` (integer id; all
  40,298 resolve to an earlier action of the same file; every observation with `tool_call_metadata` has its cause
  action's `tool_call_id`) links the result, the execution and the call. Class D (`openhands.cause_link@1`,
  `openhands.observation_is_execution@1`) where the OpenHands code that sets `cause` is verified: RedCode, whose 5,460
  logs name 1.5.0 and whose deposit vendors OpenHands 1.5.0. For OAS the user approved (2026-10-12) fetching the few source
  files of the fork commit `5a13eacf` needed to verify it; the class follows that verification (D-172 addendum). The matching
  `tool_call_id` corroborates and never raises the class. No link from order or time.
  - **Rejected:** class O for the link (the value is observed, its meaning rests on harness code, as for
    `agentdojo.call_id_unique_match`); pairing by position (no need: the explicit link exists in 100 %).
- **D-173 (2026-10-12, phase 10g: model calls and model identity; approved by the user, 2026-10-12).** `served_model`, `response_id`, `usage`
  and `finish_reason` come from `model_response` (O:provider); `request` and `t` are `not_recorded`; `input` is the logged
  prefix at class I (OAS used a browser-output condenser, so the prefix is an upper bound). Text-only agent replies have
  no response object: their call exists at class I (`openhands.text_message_is_model_output_unverified@1`); OAS gives
  their `response_id` from `llm_metrics`. `model.requested` is the `llm_metrics.token_usages[].model` string where
  recorded (OAS, e.g. `openai/neulab/claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219`); directory names only cross-check.
  - **Rejected:** model identity from directory names (the logs carry it); dropping the LiteLLM route string.
- **D-174 (2026-10-12, phase 10g: simulated users and NPCs; approved by the user, 2026-10-12).** The first user message is harness-authored
  (OAS: a fixed pointer to `/instruction/task.md`; RedCode: the generated request). Later user messages are the harness's
  simulated user: OAS `FakeUser` (an LLM, `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` in the code at the pin, for four replies, then a fixed
  text: 140 of 594 match it), RedCode one fixed text (4,421). OAS NPC replies come through the `chat` tool and keep actor
  `env`; an `npc:<name>` actor (`simulated_user`, role `npc`) is named by a SEM `author` annotation. All authorship is
  class I; NPC models are not recorded.
  - **Rejected:** attributing simulated replies to a human `user`; attributing them to the agent's environment model
    without evidence of the model.
- **D-175 (2026-10-12, phase 10g: harness steps are not tool use; approved by the user, 2026-10-12).** `recall` action and observation become a
  harness `activity` and an `artefact` (workspace context); `finish` is a control call with no execution and no
  `unexecuted_tool_call` issue; "The action has not been executed." (168 OAS, always the last event) gives no execution:
  the call is unexecuted and the notice is a harness message; the 5 uncaused `error` observations are harness errors.
  Event-id gaps (every file) are disclosed as `openhands.filtered_events`, never filled.
  - **Rejected:** mapping recall or finish as tool executions; reading the notice as a failed execution.

  container) and level 2 (member of a zip). `ingest/streams.py` `iter_zstd_bounded` parses each frame header with `struct`
  before a decoder exists: skippable frames and dictionary ids are refused (`ingest.stream.codec`: unverifiable), a window
  over `2**zstd_window_log_max` is `ingest.stream.memory`, a declared content size over the cap is `ingest.stream.size`;
  a fresh decoder per frame with `window_log_max` also set in libzstd; output bounded as it grows. Spec G.3.4/G.3.5

    one frame, window 2^23, no dictionary, 1,464,483,840 B decompressed, 75,577 entries including 1,642 GNU long names.

  bounds both tar codecs; `max_stream_bytes` keeps its meaning for the deferred single streams. `max_zstd_frames` = 1,024.

  and every slice and the envelope (streamed arrays replaced by `[]`) is parsed by `strict_json_loads` itself, so the

  (16 MiB), `max_json_elements` (1,000,000) and code `ingest.json.elements`. Accepts exactly what `strict_json_loads`
  accepts, with an equal value (property and fuzz tests). Spec G.3.3. Design §3.

  (`ingest.archive.parts`: 2..`max_split_parts` parts, none empty, each its declared size, logical size ≤ `max_split_bytes`),

  - **Why:** control-arena's three logical zips are 8 + 8 + 3 parts of 256 MiB; two are within 9,191 B of

  "agentprov-split/0.1", "parts": [{"sha256": "sha256:<hex>", "size": n}, …]}`; `store_split_descriptor` stores it;
  `ContainerSpec` checks the digest by computation; `decode_split_descriptor` reads it back strictly (canonical form
  required) for `rederive`. Member CRC checks in `verify` read member objects only, so no reassembly is needed there.

    `corpus/manifest.py` (snapshot origin kinds) and `corpus/rawtree.py` (re-mapping); the importer must call

- **D-245 (2026-10-13: calibrated budgets and limit values; a memory defect of the tar block reader fixed;
  user-approved 2026-10-13).**
  Measured as D-60 (`docs/reports/ingest-formats/calibration.md`): a zstd tar costs about 2–2.5 s worker CPU per GiB of
  stream for both passes (13× headroom at 16 GiB against 540 s); a 2 GiB split zip in 8 parts 6.8 s; streamed JSON about
  0.1 s per MB with a 32 MiB peak for 315 MB; the real `RESULTS_raw.tar.zst` 3.7 s and 77 MiB. The expand budgets and every
  proposed limit value are kept. **Defect found and fixed:** the tar block reader (D-57's, shared) grew a `bytearray` by
  reallocation per member and its peak RSS grew by one member size per member (1,733 MiB for 2 GiB selected); it now joins
  chunks once per read (324 MiB, flat; regression test).
  - **Rejected:** a tar-stream term in `with_expand_scaling` (not needed at 13× headroom; the parent does not know the
    stream size before the worker decodes it, as for D-60).

- **D-218 (2026-10-13, deferrals: carved blobs; user-approved 2026-10-13).** A mapper may store a string value of its
  primary artefact as its own raw object (C.11.5): `MapContext.carve(loc, transform)` re-derives the bytes from the
  artefact (`agentprov.raw.carve`: a key locator, the strict bounded loader, transform `utf8` or `base64` for a `data:`
  URI's payload) and returns a `$blob` reference. The map job returns the bytes as members (role `carved`); the parent
  stores them with the object-level origin `carved {from, loc, transform}` before validating the AER, after checking
  that they hash to the header and that `from` is one of the job's primary inputs (else `adapter.carve_mismatch`, a
  failed job). `rawtree`, `withhold` and `derive` treat a carved object as derived, like an archive member; `verify
  --level chain` checks that its source is stored, and a re-map carves it again. No AER schema change; no stored corpus
  moves until a mapper uses it (regen-batch item 29).
  - **Rejected:** taking the bytes from the mapper (an unverifiable claim about the source); re-carving in the parent
    or in `verify --level chain` (parsing untrusted bytes in T0, invariant 3: re-carving stays in the T1 re-map);
    storing the JSON-escaped source span instead of the value (the reference would not be the content).
  - **Addendum (2026-10-14, check-and-hold):** the parent no longer stores carved blobs before validation. It checks and
    holds them (spooled), validates each AER against the store plus the held blobs, and stores exactly those that a
    written AER lists in `seal.blobs`. A unit that falls back to a degenerate AER, a file sealed whole (D-321 refused
    rows, D-323 abort) and a filtered unit leave no carved object. `MapContext.carve` parses each source region once
    per unit (`raw.carve.Carver`). Byte-neutral.
- **D-222 (2026-10-21, deferrals: a carve reads its string by byte span; user-approved 2026-10-21; found by phase 10m's
  MCPHunt real-data trial).** A carve of a region of 8 MiB or more (`raw.carve.SPAN_MIN_BYTES`) first goes through
  `agentprov.ingest.jsonspan.string_value_at`. A byte-level walk (strings matched whole, as in `ingest.jsonstream`)
  follows the pointer to the string token. The **envelope**, the region with that token replaced by a placeholder that
  carries the region's own SHA-256, and the token alone are each parsed by `strict_json_loads`, and the pointer must
  resolve to the placeholder in the parsed envelope. The region is valid exactly when both parses succeed, so the strict
  rules are unchanged. Anything the path cannot prove falls back to the whole parse, so the carved bytes and every
  refusal are the same. A `Carver` keeps no parsed copy of such a region.
  - **Why:** `mitigation/minimax_m3_rv1.json` (52.7 MiB) has a 46.9 MB trace with a 43.6 MB `result_full`. Re-parsing
    the trace's byte range while the reader's parsed copy was alive (and keeping it cached) stopped the map job at
    `worker.limit.rss` (2 GiB), so the document sealed as one degenerate AER. On a synthetic document of that shape,
    the carve's traced peak falls from 661 to 165 MiB (ASCII) and from 807 to 406 MiB (with a 4-byte character), and
    the memory kept after it from 99 to 42 MiB and from 214 to 42 MiB.
  - **Byte-neutral:** no locator, origin, AER, PROV or format changes. `ingest/` and `raw/` are in no stage
    `engine_code_sha256`, so no digest moves. Verify and re-map carve through the same function.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a second, streaming JSON parser for carving (a parser differential on untrusted bytes; the strict loader stays
      the only judge);
    - a raised map cap only (it moves the limit; MCPHunt documents reach 110.9 MB);
    - carving an escape-free string's bytes directly (a second validator of JSON string rules, for little gain on
      escape-heavy tool results).
- **D-220 (2026-10-14, deferrals: `import --fetch` serves a cached pin offline; user-approved 2026-10-14, regen-plan
  finding F-7).** `import --fetch` no longer needs `--allow-network` when the pin is cached: without it the Fetcher runs
  offline (`allow_network=False`, as `raw.fetch` already does), a cached pin is imported with no socket opened and no
  acquisitions row, and an uncached one is refused with `raw.fetch.not_cached` (exit 4, the N.1.11 refusal). With
  `--allow-network` nothing changes. The unused `cli.refused.network` error is removed. Byte-neutral; it lets the
  regeneration round (route (a)) re-import the six git-pinned corpora offline from the cache with git origins (O-1).
  - **Rejected:** keeping the CLI gate stricter than the Fetcher (a network flag for an offline read); a new flag for
    offline reads (the default already is the offline behaviour).
